@@ -0,0 +1,364 @@
+# SDK Metrics — Design
+
+## Goal
+
+Instrument the DXOS SDK with a small, fixed set of OTel metrics that answer five
+operational questions about the deployed client fleet, and surface them on a
+SigNoz dashboard:
+
+1. How many spaces does a client hold?
+2. How often does the EDGE websocket reconnect?
+3. How many documents does a client have loaded?
+4. **Is sync stuck** — what is the longest stretch a client takes to reach a
+   synced state, and how long has a client been unsynced without making
+   progress?
+5. How much memory does a client use, and how close is it to the heap limit?
+
+Non-goals: tracing changes, log volume changes, per-space or per-object
+drilldown (see [Cardinality budget](#cardinality-budget)).
+
+## What already exists
+
+The whole SDK → OTel → OTLP → SigNoz path is built and enabled in Composer.
+This project adds instruments to it; it does not build the pipeline.
+
+| Piece                                | Location                                                                                                                                  |
+| ------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
+| Collector-free SDK facade            | `RemoteMetrics` in `packages/common/tracing/src/remote/metrics.ts`, exposed as `trace.metrics` (`packages/common/tracing/src/api.ts:203`) |
+| OTel meter + OTLP exporter           | `OtelMetrics` in `packages/sdk/observability/src/extensions/otel/metrics.ts` — registers itself as a `RemoteMetrics` processor            |
+| Endpoint / resource / tag resolution | `packages/sdk/observability/src/extensions/otel/extension.ts`                                                                             |
+| Metric producers                     | `packages/sdk/observability/src/providers/client-observability.ts`                                                                        |
+| Provider registration                | `packages/plugins/plugin-observability/src/capabilities/client-ready.ts:48-60`                                                            |
+| Enabled for Composer                 | `packages/apps/composer-app/src/util/config.ts:90` (`metrics: true`)                                                                      |
+
+## The two emission contracts
+
+Deep SDK packages have no `Observability` handle, so there are two paths and the
+choice is mechanical:
+
+1. **`trace.metrics` (`@dxos/tracing`)** — for anything inside `@dxos/edge-client`,
+   `@dxos/echo-client`, `@dxos/echo-host`. Zero OTel dependency; fans out to zero
+   processors until `OtelMetrics` registers one, so no-collector means no cost and
+   telemetry opt-out is "never register". **These packages must never depend on
+   `@dxos/observability`.**
+2. **`observability.metrics` via a `DataProvider`** — for anything that needs the
+   `Client` API surface (space counts, aggregated sync state). Lives in
+   `packages/sdk/observability/src/providers/`.
+
+`trace.metrics` is currently dead code — nothing in the SDK calls it. This project
+is its first real consumer.
+
+## Prerequisite exporter fixes
+
+These are defects in the existing exporter config that would corrupt or bloat the
+new metrics. They land before the instruments.
+
+### P1 — Delta temporality
+
+`OTLPMetricExporter` is constructed with no `temporalityPreference`, so counters
+and histograms export **cumulative**. Browser clients are short-lived and reload
+constantly; a cumulative counter restarting at 0 every reload reads as a counter
+reset in SigNoz and corrupts every `rate`/`increase` panel. Set delta temporality
+for counters and histograms.
+
+### P2 — Drop `session.id` from the metrics resource
+
+`extension.ts` stamps `'session.id': crypto.randomUUID()` as a **resource**
+attribute, so it lands on metrics as well as traces/logs. SigNoz stores metrics as
+`(fingerprint, unix_milli, value)` in ClickHouse `samples_v4` keyed on the full
+label set — a fresh UUID per page reload mints a permanent new fingerprint whose
+samples never merge with anything. Compression (Gorilla + ZSTD on values) does
+nothing about series count. Keep `session.id` on traces and logs; drop it from
+metrics.
+
+The fix must be a **separate resource for the metrics provider**, not a `View`.
+`extension.ts` builds one resource and hands the same object to `OtelLogs`,
+`OtelMetrics`, and `OtelTraces`; `OtelMetrics` passes it straight to
+`MeterProvider`. OTel `View`s filter _datapoint attributes_ via `attributeKeys` —
+they have no reach into provider-level resource attributes, so a view cannot strip
+this. If a custom exporter transform is used instead, it needs an exported-payload
+test asserting `session.id` is absent from metrics and present on traces and logs.
+
+### P3 — Cache instruments
+
+`OtelMetrics.gauge/increment/distribution` call `createGauge(name)` /
+`createCounter(name)` on **every** record. The SDK dedupes by descriptor so it is
+correct, but it allocates per call on a hot path. Hold a `Map<string, Instrument>`.
+
+### P4 — `observe()` on `RemoteMetrics`
+
+`MetricsMethods` is push-only, which is why the existing providers poll on a
+10-minute timer while `EXPORT_INTERVAL` is 60s — 9 of every 10 export windows carry
+no datapoint, producing sparse series that break `avg`/percentile panels. Add:
+
+```ts
+observe(name: string, callback: () => number | undefined, data?: MetricData): CleanupFn;
+```
+
+mapped to `createObservableGauge` in `OtelMetrics`, so "current value" metrics are
+read at collection time. **Every gauge in this project uses `observe`, not
+`gauge`.** Existing `dxos.client.network.*` / `dxos.client.runtime.*` gauges are
+migrated opportunistically, not as a blocker.
+
+### P5 — Honor `unit` and `description`
+
+`MetricData.unit` exists and is dropped on the floor by `OtelMetrics`. Pass it
+through, and add `description`. Also register explicit histogram bucket boundaries
+via a `View` — the OTel default boundaries top out at 10,000 and are shaped for
+milliseconds, which is wrong for the seconds-to-minutes durations below.
+
+## Metrics to add
+
+Names follow the existing `dxos.<subsystem>.…` convention. Units use UCUM as OTel
+requires (`s` for seconds, `{thing}` for dimensionless counts).
+
+### Spaces
+
+| Metric                           | Instrument       | Unit      | Attributes | Source                                                |
+| -------------------------------- | ---------------- | --------- | ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
+| `dxos.client.spaces.count`       | observable gauge | `{space}` | —          | `client.spaces.get().length`                          |
+| `dxos.client.spaces.ready.count` | observable gauge | `{space}` | —          | spaces whose `state.get() === SpaceState.SPACE_READY` |
+
+Read at collection time in `spacesMetricsProvider`
+(`providers/client-observability.ts:165`). The gap between the two is the
+"spaces known but not opened" signal.
+
+The same change **removes the `key: data.key` attribute** from the existing
+`dxos.client.space.members` / `.objects` / `.epoch` /
+`.currentDataMutations` gauges — that attribute is one series per space per
+device, i.e. unbounded in the number of spaces users create. Per-space drilldown
+is a traces/logs question, not a metrics one.
+
+### EDGE websocket
+
+| Metric                          | Instrument       | Unit          | Attributes                 | Source                                                     |
+| ------------------------------- | ---------------- | ------------- | -------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
+| `dxos.edge.ws.reconnect.count`  | counter (delta)  | `{reconnect}` | `reason`                   | `EdgeClient` reconnect notification (`edge-client.ts:355`) |
+| `dxos.edge.ws.connected`        | observable gauge | `1`           | —                          | 1 while the connection is open, else 0                     |
+| `dxos.edge.ws.connect.duration` | histogram        | `s`           | `outcome=success\|failure` | dial start → open / failure                                |
+
+`reason` must be a **bounded** enum derived from the close code / error class
+(`normal`, `going_away`, `abnormal`, `network`, `auth`, `identity_changed`,
+`other`) — never a raw error message. Emitted via `trace.metrics` from
+`packages/core/mesh/edge-client/src/edge-client.ts`.
+
+`dxos.edge.ws.connected` as a gauge lets a single SigNoz panel show fleet
+connectivity (`avg` across series = fraction of clients online), which a counter
+cannot.
+
+Suggested buckets for `connect.duration`: `[0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10, 30, 60]`.
+
+### Documents
+
+| Metric                               | Instrument       | Unit         | Attributes               | Source                                                          |
+| ------------------------------------ | ---------------- | ------------ | ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
+| `dxos.echo.documents.count`          | observable gauge | `{document}` | `location=local\|remote` | `getSyncSummary()` `localDocumentCount` / `remoteDocumentCount` |
+| `dxos.echo.documents.unsynced.count` | observable gauge | `{document}` | —                        | `getSyncSummary().unsyncedDocumentCount`                        |
+
+`getSyncSummary` (`packages/sdk/client/src/echo/util.ts:23`) already folds
+per-space `SpaceSyncState.PeerState` into a single fleet-comparable summary, so
+this is a read of data the client already maintains. `localDocumentCount` is the
+"documents loaded" number.
+
+> A _count of load events_ (as opposed to a resident count) would need a counter
+> at the repo `find`/load boundary in `@dxos/echo-host`. Deliberately out of scope
+> — the resident gauge answers the operational question and the load boundary is a
+> much deeper change.
+
+### Sync (the interesting one)
+
+Both instruments are needed; neither alone answers the question.
+
+| Metric                            | Instrument       | Unit | Attributes | Source                                                      |
+| --------------------------------- | ---------------- | ---- | ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
+| `dxos.echo.sync.episode.duration` | histogram        | `s`  | —          | recorded on the `unsynced > 0` → `unsynced == 0` transition |
+| `dxos.echo.sync.stalled.duration` | observable gauge | `s`  | —          | `now − lastProgressAt` while unsynced; `0` when synced      |
+
+**`episode.duration`** — "the longest stretch of time it takes a client to sync".
+A _sync episode_ opens when `getSyncSummary().unsyncedDocumentCount` goes from 0
+to non-zero and closes when it returns to 0; the histogram records the episode's
+wall-clock duration. Because OTel exports explicit-bucket histograms, SigNoz merges
+buckets across every client before computing the statistic — so `max` gives the
+worst episode in the fleet and `p99` the tail, and neither can be obtained from a
+client-computed percentile (percentiles are not mergeable; bucket counts are).
+
+**`stalled.duration`** — "the time the client has been unsynced without progress".
+This is the stuck-detector, and it is why the histogram is not sufficient: an
+episode that _never closes_ never records a histogram sample, so a permanently
+stuck client is invisible in `episode.duration` by construction. The gauge is read
+at collection time and reports the age of the last observed decrease in
+`unsyncedDocumentCount`. `> 600` while `documents.unsynced.count > 0` is the
+alertable condition.
+
+Progress is defined as a **decrease in `unsyncedDocumentCount`**, not any state
+emission — otherwise a client that keeps re-reporting the same backlog looks
+healthy. Note that a client concurrently _creating_ documents raises the count, so
+the definition tracks the low-water mark within the episode rather than the raw
+value.
+
+**First-sample policy (startup and reload).** An episode opens on a
+`0 → non-zero` transition, but a provider that starts — or a tab that reloads —
+with `unsyncedDocumentCount` already non-zero never sees that transition. Without
+a rule, the in-flight episode is invisible to both instruments. The rule:
+
+- On the **first observation** with `unsynced > 0`, open an episode with
+  `openedAt = lastProgressAt = now`. Both are lower bounds: the backlog may have
+  existed for hours before the process started.
+- `stalled.duration` therefore starts from 0 at startup and becomes meaningful
+  after one collection interval. It never returns "unknown" — a stuck client is
+  visible within a minute of boot either way.
+- A truncated episode **is** recorded to the histogram when it closes, accepting
+  that it under-reports duration. The alternative — an `origin=observed|truncated`
+  attribute — doubles the histogram's series count (see
+  [Cardinality budget](#cardinality-budget), where histograms already dominate)
+  to fix a bias the `stalled.duration` gauge already covers. Document the bias
+  instead of paying for it.
+- Episode state is **not persisted across reloads**. Persisting it would need
+  storage plus a clock-skew story, and the gauge makes a genuinely stuck client
+  visible regardless. Explicitly out of scope.
+
+Suggested buckets for `episode.duration`:
+`[1, 5, 15, 30, 60, 120, 300, 600, 1800, 3600]`.
+
+Source of truth is `db.subscribeToSyncState(cb, options)`
+(`packages/core/echo/echo-client/src/proxy-db/database.ts:778`), **not** the
+automerge-only `subscribeToAutomergeSyncState` path `useSyncState` uses. Since
+#12561 landed it already selects the EDGE peer and owns its own no-change poll
+backoff (2s, doubling to a 15s ceiling, snapping back the moment the backlog
+moves), so a `DataProvider` consuming it needs no timer of its own — which is
+what the earlier "must not own a poll" constraint was waiting for.
+
+`Database.SyncState` also covers **feed blocks** (`blocksToPull`, `blocksToPush`,
+`totalBlocks`) alongside documents. An episode is therefore defined over total
+pending work, `unsyncedDocumentCount + blocksToPull + blocksToPush`, matching how
+`toSpaceUpdate` (`packages/plugins/plugin-client/src/progress/space-sync-progress.ts`)
+already decides a space is caught up. A client with a stalled feed backlog is
+stuck whether or not its documents converged, so scoping the episode to documents
+would miss it. The `dxos.echo.documents.*` gauges stay document-only.

+| Provider registration                | `packages/plugins/plugin-observability/src/capabilities/client-ready.ts:48-60`                                                            |

+   telemetry opt-out is "never register". **These packages must never depend on
+   `@dxos/observability`.**

+   `Client` API surface (space counts, aggregated sync state). Lives in

+and histograms export **cumulative**. Browser clients are short-lived and reload

+test asserting `session.id` is absent from metrics and present on traces and logs.

+`createCounter(name)` on **every** record. The SDK dedupes by descriptor so it is

+read at collection time. **Every gauge in this project uses `observe`, not
+`gauge`.** Existing `dxos.client.network.*` / `dxos.client.runtime.*` gauges are
+migrated opportunistically, not as a blocker.

+device, i.e. unbounded in the number of spaces users create. Per-space drilldown
+is a traces/logs question, not a metrics one.

+
+| Metric                          | Instrument       | Unit          | Attributes                 | Source                                                     |
+| ------------------------------- | ---------------- | ------------- | -------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
+| `dxos.edge.ws.reconnect.count`  | counter (delta)  | `{reconnect}` | `reason`                   | `EdgeClient` reconnect notification (`edge-client.ts:355`) |

+`packages/core/mesh/edge-client/src/edge-client.ts`.

+`dxos.edge.ws.connected` as a gauge lets a single SigNoz panel show fleet
+connectivity (`avg` across series = fraction of clients online), which a counter
+cannot.
+
+Suggested buckets for `connect.duration`: `[0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10, 30, 60]`.
+
+### Documents
+
+| Metric                               | Instrument       | Unit         | Attributes               | Source                                                          |
+| ------------------------------------ | ---------------- | ------------ | ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
+| `dxos.echo.documents.count`          | observable gauge | `{document}` | `location=local\|remote` | `getSyncSummary()` `localDocumentCount` / `remoteDocumentCount` |
+| `dxos.echo.documents.unsynced.count` | observable gauge | `{document}` | —                        | `getSyncSummary().unsyncedDocumentCount`                        |
+
+`getSyncSummary` (`packages/sdk/client/src/echo/util.ts:23`) already folds
+per-space `SpaceSyncState.PeerState` into a single fleet-comparable summary, so
+this is a read of data the client already maintains. `localDocumentCount` is the
+"documents loaded" number.
+
+> A _count of load events_ (as opposed to a resident count) would need a counter
+> at the repo `find`/load boundary in `@dxos/echo-host`. Deliberately out of scope
+> — the resident gauge answers the operational question and the load boundary is a
+> much deeper change.
+
+### Sync (the interesting one)
+
+Both instruments are needed; neither alone answers the question.
+
+| Metric                            | Instrument       | Unit | Attributes | Source                                                      |
+| --------------------------------- | ---------------- | ---- | ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
+| `dxos.echo.sync.episode.duration` | histogram        | `s`  | —          | recorded on the `unsynced > 0` → `unsynced == 0` transition |
+| `dxos.echo.sync.stalled.duration` | observable gauge | `s`  | —          | `now − lastProgressAt` while unsynced; `0` when synced      |
+
+**`episode.duration`** — "the longest stretch of time it takes a client to sync".
+A _sync episode_ opens when `getSyncSummary().unsyncedDocumentCount` goes from 0
+to non-zero and closes when it returns to 0; the histogram records the episode's
+wall-clock duration. Because OTel exports explicit-bucket histograms, SigNoz merges
+buckets across every client before computing the statistic — so `max` gives the
+worst episode in the fleet and `p99` the tail, and neither can be obtained from a
+client-computed percentile (percentiles are not mergeable; bucket counts are).
+
+**`stalled.duration`** — "the time the client has been unsynced without progress".
+This is the stuck-detector, and it is why the histogram is not sufficient: an
+episode that _never closes_ never records a histogram sample, so a permanently
+stuck client is invisible in `episode.duration` by construction. The gauge is read
+at collection time and reports the age of the last observed decrease in
+`unsyncedDocumentCount`. `> 600` while `documents.unsynced.count > 0` is the
+alertable condition.
+
+Progress is defined as a **decrease in `unsyncedDocumentCount`**, not any state
+emission — otherwise a client that keeps re-reporting the same backlog looks
+healthy. Note that a client concurrently _creating_ documents raises the count, so
+the definition tracks the low-water mark within the episode rather than the raw
+value.
+

+`0 → non-zero` transition, but a provider that starts — or a tab that reloads —
+with `unsyncedDocumentCount` already non-zero never sees that transition. Without
+a rule, the in-flight episode is invisible to both instruments. The rule:
+

+  `openedAt = lastProgressAt = now`. Both are lower bounds: the backlog may have
+  existed for hours before the process started.
+- `stalled.duration` therefore starts from 0 at startup and becomes meaningful
+  after one collection interval. It never returns "unknown" — a stuck client is
+  visible within a minute of boot either way.

+  that it under-reports duration. The alternative — an `origin=observed|truncated`
+  attribute — doubles the histogram's series count (see
+  [Cardinality budget](#cardinality-budget), where histograms already dominate)
+  to fix a bias the `stalled.duration` gauge already covers. Document the bias
+  instead of paying for it.
+- Episode state is **not persisted across reloads**. Persisting it would need
+  storage plus a clock-skew story, and the gauge makes a genuinely stuck client
+  visible regardless. Explicitly out of scope.

+`[1, 5, 15, 30, 60, 120, 300, 600, 1800, 3600]`.

+automerge-only `subscribeToAutomergeSyncState` path `useSyncState` uses. Since

+  - `unregisterProcessor` detaches a collector and its observations on shutdown,
+    called from `OtelMetrics.close()` before provider shutdown. Without it a closed
+    processor kept receiving samples, later observations attached to its dead
+    provider, and a re-initialized collector double-reported alongside it.
+  - 9 unit tests in `remote/metrics.test.ts` (fan-out, replay, double-register,
+    cleanup across late processors, no-processor no-op, unregister, idempotent
+    unregister, close-and-reinitialize).
+- [x] **Pass `unit`/`description` through, register histogram `View`s** (P5) — added
+      `description` to `MetricData` and a `MetricMeta` param on the extension API;
+      instruments are created with both. Two non-overlapping explicit-bucket views
+      registered for the Phase 3/4 histograms (inert until those instruments exist —
+      two matching views would produce duplicate streams, so there is no catch-all).
+  - Also tightened `tags?: any` to `Attributes` and made `convertTags` drop nullish
+    values, which are not valid OTel attribute values.

+`packages/sdk/observability/src/providers/client-observability.ts`.

+      `spacesMetricsProvider`, reading `client.spaces.get()` fresh at each collection

+      `dxos.client.space.*` gauges now report device-wide totals.
+  - `members`/`objects`/`currentDataMutations` sum; `epoch` takes the **max**, since
+    epochs are per-space sequence numbers and adding them means nothing.
+- [x] **`dxos.echo.documents.count{location=local|remote}` + `dxos.echo.documents.unsynced.count`**
+      — new `documentsMetricsProvider`, registered in `plugin-observability`.
+  - Sourced from `db.subscribeToSyncState` via the new `providers/sync-state.ts`, not
+    `getSyncSummary` as originally planned: only the former sees feed blocks, and it
+    already owns its poll backoff (see Phase 4).
+  - `subscribeSyncSummary` is the shared tracker Phase 4 extends; `foldSyncStates` is
+    split out as a pure function and unit-tested (5 tests, no mocks).
+- [x] **Migrate the existing heap gauges to `observe()` and declare `By` units** — all six
+      moved off the 10-minute push timer; names unchanged so SigNoz history is not orphaned.
+  - `dxos.client.runtime.*` reads `performance.memory` synchronously at collection time.
+  - `dxos.client.services.runtime.*` cannot: it is an RPC. Sampled on a 30s cadence
+    (under the 60s export, so a collection never reads a stale sample) with the gauge
+    reading the latest value, which keeps the `observe` contract synchronous.

+    the scopes still sum to the total the browser reported. `foldBreakdown` is pure and
+    unit-tested (5 tests).

+  - Registry entry owned by jdw; it set the 300-400MB resting target and the
+    `scripts/memory/soak.mjs` harness. This phase makes that target verifiable
+    fleet-wide instead of on one machine.

Done — the contract now lives in both documents. Added a "Fleet-wide memory metrics" section to `.agents/projects/memory-usage/TASKS.md` with the series table, units and `scope` values, plus the two decisions a panel author needs: the resting-target panel reads `dxos.client.runtime.heapUsed` rather than `memory.bytes` (the latter is feature-detected behind cross-origin isolation, so its series is absent for some clients and a target built on it would silently under-report), and heap pressure is `heapUsed / heapSizeLimit` computed at query time rather than a third exported series. body:
Done in `d1986116` — the scan is gone. Two things blocked the index path, both fixed here:

1. **The index didn't cover named entities.** `extractReferences` dropped every non-`echo:` reference, so `dxn:` targets were absent entirely. A `dxn:` reference is now keyed by its **unversioned** NSID, so one lookup finds every version of a name; the referencing object still holds the versioned URI, which is what the rewrite reads. Echo refs keep their local-form normalization. No table change (the column was already `TEXT`), but existing databases hold no `dxn:` rows — so a cursor-clearing migration (`indexCursor`, `indexName = 'reverseRef'`) makes the next pass re-scan, following the precedent in `0001_init.sql`.

2. **No client-reachable lookup by DXN.** An `incoming-references` clause can only anchor on an entity in the working set (`_anchorTargetDxn` derives an `EID` from a `QueryItem`), and a named entity never is one. Rather than extend the AST, planner, plan steps and both executors, this adds `QueryService.queryReverseRef`. Its handler awaits `updateIndexes()` first, so a caller that just wrote an object doesn't read a stale set.

`#runRenameMigration` now asks the index for the referencing objects and loads only those.

The 8 rename tests run client → RPC → index, so they double as proof that `dxn:` targets are indexed and that the unversioned key resolves the versioned reference in the fixture; `reverse-ref-index.test.ts` gained a unit test for the key normalization. `index-core` 48/48, `echo-host` 293, `echo-client` 554 all pass.

+# Audit: remaining protobuf.js dependencies and cost of migrating to buf

+Status: audit only — no code changes. Counts taken from `main` at the time of writing.

+
+| Package                   | Role                                                                     | Source LOC |
+| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------- |
+| `@dxos/codec-protobuf`    | runtime: codecs, substitutions, `Stream`, service descriptors            | 1,599      |
+| `@dxos/protobuf-compiler` | build-time codegen (`build-protobuf`) producing `src/proto/gen`          | 1,368      |
+| `@dxos/effect-proto`      | protobuf descriptor → Effect Schema conversion (used by `react-ui-form`) | 415        |
+
+Everything else depends on protobuf.js transitively, through generated types imported from
+`@dxos/protocols/proto/*` and through `@dxos/codec-protobuf` at runtime.
+
+Codegen is **not** the blocker: `@dxos/protocols` already runs `buf generate` (`buf.gen.yaml`,
+`protoc-gen-es`) over the _same_ `src/proto` tree in its `gen-buf` task, so a `@bufbuild/protobuf`
+message type already exists for all 220 messages in the 51 `.proto` files (3,737 LOC). The two
+generators run side by side and both outputs are consumed today.

+## Current exposure

+| Surface                                                                  | Count                        |
+| ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------- |
+| `.ts`/`.tsx` files importing `@dxos/protocols/proto/*` (protobuf.js gen) | 275 files / 409 declarations |
+| Files importing `@dxos/protocols/buf/*` (already migrated)               | 25 (dxos) + 85 (edge)        |
+| Files importing `@dxos/codec-protobuf`                                   | 39                           |
+| `schema.getCodecForType(...)` call sites                                 | 47                           |
+| `Stream` imports from `@dxos/codec-protobuf`                             | 26                           |

+Counted over git-tracked `*.ts`/`*.tsx` only, matching `import`/`export … from '@dxos/protocols/proto/…'`
+declarations (not raw mentions of the path, which come to 464 lines). How many of those declarations
+touch a _substituted_ field is not measured here — it needs per-field analysis, and it is the number
+that actually sizes the sweep.
+
+Heaviest legacy consumers (files importing `@dxos/protocols/proto/*`):
+`sdk/client-services` (83), `core/mesh` (50), `core/halo` (28), `sdk/client` (23),
+`devtools/devtools` (19), `plugins/plugin-space` (11).

+Most-imported legacy modules: `dxos/client/services` (106), `dxos/halo/credentials` (94),

+`dxos/edge` adds one direct dependent (`@dxos/hub-protocol` → `@dxos/codec-protobuf`) plus
+17 files still importing `@dxos/protocols/proto/*`; its newer code already uses
+`@dxos/protocols/buf/*` for credentials, keys, query and messenger.
+
+## What actually has to be replaced
+
+Codegen is solved; the cost is concentrated in four runtime behaviours protobuf.js gives us and
+`@bufbuild/protobuf` does not:
+
+1. **Substitutions.** `packages/core/protocols/src/proto/substitutions.ts` rewrites
+   `dxos.keys.PublicKey` → `PublicKey`, `dxos.keys.PrivateKey` → `Buffer`,
+   `dxos.echo.timeframe.TimeframeVector` → `Timeframe`, plus `Any`, `Struct` and `Timestamp`
+   handling. Generated buf types are plain messages, so every one of the 409 import sites that
+   touches a substituted field sees a different shape (`{ data: Uint8Array }` instead of a
+   `PublicKey` instance). This is the bulk of the mechanical work.
+2. **Credential signature stability.** `credentials/src/credentials/signing.ts` signs
+   `json-stable-stringify` of the _substituted object_, not the wire bytes. Any change to the
+   decoded object shape (Timestamp as `Date` vs `{seconds,nanos}`, `PublicKey` instance vs

+   shim that reproduces the current JSON exactly is mandatory, and
+   `presentations/json-encoding.test.ts` already documents the divergence

+3. **Persisted data.** `dxos.halo.keyring.KeyRecord` (SQLite keyring),

+4. **Service descriptors and `Stream`.** `@dxos/rpc` (`ServiceBundle`, `createProtoRpcPeer`,
+   ~60 call sites) is built on protobuf.js `ServiceDescriptor`; 18 `service {}` blocks with 36
+   rpc methods. `Stream` is a bespoke type re-exported from `codec-protobuf` in 26 places.

+The client-services RPC layer is already being moved off protobuf.js _service descriptors_ onto
+`effect/unstable/rpc` with hand-authored `effect/Schema` payloads

+| Phase | Work                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Estimate    |
+| ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- |
+| 0     | Shape-compat layer: buf-based encode/decode that reproduces the current substituted object shape (PublicKey/PrivateKey/Timeframe/Any/Struct/Timestamp), with round-trip and byte-equality tests against protobuf.js | 1–1.5 weeks |

+touches most of the repo. Phases 0–2 (~3 weeks) deliver the actual de-risking; stopping after

+//
+// Copyright 2026 DXOS.org
+//
+
+// Encodes and decodes buf (`@bufbuild/protobuf`) messages using the same JS object shapes the
+// protobuf.js codec produces, so call sites can move to buf one at a time without every
+// substituted field changing type under them.
+//
+// The substitutions this mirrors live in `src/proto/substitutions.ts` (PublicKey, PrivateKey,
+// TimeframeVector) plus `@dxos/codec-protobuf`'s well-known-type substitutions (Struct,
+// Timestamp). `google.protobuf.Any` is NOT handled here: the protobuf.js version resolves the
+// payload through the schema registry via an `@type` discriminator and honours the `preserve_any`
+// field option, which needs a buf-side type registry — see `docs/audits/protobufjs-to-buf.md`.
+
+import {
+  type DescField,
+  type DescMessage,
+  type Message,
+  ScalarType,
+  create,
+  fromBinary,
+  toBinary,
+} from '@bufbuild/protobuf';
+
+import { PublicKey } from '@dxos/keys';
+import { Timeframe } from '@dxos/timeframe';
+
+/**
+ * Thrown when a message reaches the compat layer carrying a field whose protobuf.js shape cannot
+ * be reproduced on buf. Failing loudly beats silently writing a differently-shaped value into
+ * persisted or signed data.
+ */
+export class UnsupportedSubstitutionError extends Error {
+  constructor(typeName: string) {
+    super(`No buf shape-compat substitution for ${typeName}.`);
+  }
+}
+
+type Substitution = {
+  /** Substituted JS value -> plain object accepted by the buf message constructor. */
+  readonly toProto: (value: any) => unknown;
+  /** Decoded buf message -> substituted JS value. */
+  readonly fromProto: (value: any) => unknown;
+};
+
+const publicKeySubstitution: Substitution = {
+  toProto: (value: PublicKey) => ({ data: value.asUint8Array() }),
+  fromProto: (value: any) => PublicKey.from(value.data),
+};
+
+const substitutions: Record<string, Substitution> = {
+  'dxos.keys.PublicKey': publicKeySubstitution,
+
+  // Matches the legacy substitution: encoded from a Buffer, decoded back to one.
+  'dxos.keys.PrivateKey': {
+    toProto: (value: Buffer) => ({ data: new Uint8Array(value) }),
+    fromProto: (value: any) => PublicKey.from(new Uint8Array(value.data)).asBuffer(),
+  },
+
+  'dxos.echo.timeframe.TimeframeVector': {
+    toProto: (timeframe: Timeframe) => ({
+      frames: timeframe.frames().map(([feedKey, seq]) => ({ feedKey: feedKey.asUint8Array(), seq })),
+    }),
+    fromProto: (value: any) =>
+      new Timeframe(
+        (value.frames ?? [])
+          .filter((frame: any) => frame.feedKey != null && frame.seq != null)
+          .map((frame: any) => [PublicKey.from(frame.feedKey), frame.seq]),
+      ),
+  },
+
+  'google.protobuf.Struct': {
+    toProto: (value: Record<string, any>) => encodeStruct(value),
+    fromProto: (value: any) => decodeStruct(value),
+  },
+
+  // protobuf.js renders a Timestamp as a Date; buf's generated type keeps seconds as a bigint,
+  // so the seconds/nanos split is reproduced rather than reused.
+  'google.protobuf.Timestamp': {
+    toProto: (value: Date) => {
+      const unixMilliseconds = value.getTime();
+      return {
+        seconds: BigInt(Math.floor(unixMilliseconds / 1000)),
+        nanos: (unixMilliseconds % 1000) * 1e6,
+      };
body:
Fixed in d89f140 — good catch, this was a real bug. `nanos` now derives from the floored-seconds boundary, so `new Date(-1)` gives `seconds: -1n`, `nanos: 999_000_000` as you specified. Regression test added (5/5 passing).

Worth recording why this is a deliberate divergence rather than a straight fix: the legacy `codec-protobuf` substitution uses the same `ms % 1000 * 1e6` formula, so before this change both codecs produced byte-identical *and equally wrong* output — I probed it, and `new Date(-1)` round-trips through protobuf.js as `1969-12-31T23:59:58.999Z`, a second early. The compat layer's job is shape parity, but reproducing a value corruption into new code is worse than diverging, so it now canonicalises and the audit documents the divergence.

The same probe turned up a second divergence I've now documented: protobuf.js materialises unset non-optional message fields as empty submessages where buf omits them (`Invitation` without `swarm_key` gains a `42 02 0a 00` run). Wire-compatible, not byte-identical — so byte equality holds only once those fields are set, which is why it doesn't affect the two messages migrated here.

body:
Good catch — both gaps are real, and worse than they look. Confirmed empirically against `@changesets/parse@1.0.0` (the version `pnpm-lock.yaml` pins):

| Front matter | old regex saw | parser sees |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{ '@dxos/echo': major }` | *nothing* | `major` |
| `'@dxos/composer-app': none` + `'@dxos/echo': patch` | echo only | **both** → mixed |

So a `major` written as a flow mapping bypassed the rule that exists to stop a 1.0.0 cut across the whole fixed group, and a `none` release hid exactly the mixed-ignored changeset this gate was added for. (Both pre-date this PR — inherited from `BUMP_LINE` in `check-changeset-bumps.mjs`.)

Fixed in b86625fa, but **without** taking `@changesets/parse` as a direct dependency. Declaring it means regenerating `pnpm-lock.yaml`, and this sandbox has only Node 20/21/22 while the repo requires `^24.0.0` — `pnpm install --lockfile-only` under Node 22 produced 164 lines of unrelated peer-resolution churn (`zod` and `@types/node` keys shifting on `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` and others), against 0 lines from a pristine tree. That is not something to push into a PR whose job is unblocking `publish`.

What went in instead, keeping the script dependency-free:

- accept `none`;
- reject the bare `@`-scoped name (`@dxos/echo: patch`), which `parseChangesetFile` itself throws on as invalid YAML — the old regex accepted it;
- **make an unreadable front-matter line a failure rather than an empty release list.** This is the load-bearing part: a flow mapping now fails loudly instead of passing silently. A gate that sees no releases in a file it does not understand passes the very changeset it exists to reject, so it no longer gets to shrug.

Validated against the real parser over all 177 changesets in the tree — identical releases for all 177, zero disagreements.

Adopting `parseChangesetFile` is still the better long-term shape and worth a follow-up that can run the install on Node 24. It needs a `try`/`catch` regardless: v1.0.0 exports only `parseChangesetFile`, not `safeParseChangesetFile`, and the count rule's `# multiple-changesets:` waiver has to keep its own front-matter read, since the parser drops comments by design.

body:
Taken as originally suggested in 120d34ac — `parseChangesetFile` now reads every release entry, with `@changesets/parse` declared through the catalog.

**Correcting my previous reply:** I attributed the lockfile churn to resolving under Node 22 instead of the pinned 24.11.1. That was wrong. Downloading Node 24.11.1 and re-resolving produced a byte-identical 166-line diff, and adding an unrelated zero-dependency package (`ms@2.1.3`) reproduces the same ~160 lines. It is pre-existing drift in `pnpm-lock.yaml` that any full re-resolve surfaces — nothing to do with this dependency or with the Node version. So there was no good reason to avoid the dependency, and the lockfile is regenerated with `pnpm install --lockfile-only` under the pinned Node.

The parser turns out to be better than "closes the two holes". It reports the violation instead of refusing the file:

| Front matter | regex version | parser |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{ '@dxos/echo': major }` | "cannot read this line" | fails as a **`major` bump** |
| `{ '@dxos/echo': patch }` | rejected — false positive | **passes** (it is valid YAML) |
| `'@dxos/echo': enormous` | zero releases → passed | `invalid version type "enormous"` |
| `'@dxos/composer-app': none` + `'@dxos/echo': patch` | echo only | mixed, correctly rejected |

Two details worth recording for anyone touching this later:

1. `@changesets/parse@1.0.0` exports only `parseChangesetFile`, not `safeParseChangesetFile`, so the call is wrapped and a throw becomes a reported parse failure. That rule runs first — every other rule reasons about the releases a changeset declares, so a file whose releases were never read would quietly satisfy all of them.
2. `frontMatter` survives, for the count rule's `# multiple-changesets:` waiver only. The parser discards comments by design, which is exactly why the waiver is one — it must never reach `CHANGELOG.md`.

+#!/usr/bin/env node
+//
+// Copyright 2026 DXOS.org
+//
+
+// Regenerate the macOS app icon from the shared full-bleed artwork.
+//
+// macOS renders an app icon exactly as given — unlike iOS, it applies no mask, and `tauri icon` adds no
+// margin either — so the rounded tile and the margin around it have to be drawn into the artwork or the
+// dock shows a hard square that also sits taller than its neighbours.
+//
+// This runs as its own pass rather than inside `gen-icon-variants.mjs` because the shape must NOT reach
+// the other platforms: iOS masks the icon itself (a pre-rounded source gets double-rounded, leaving dark
+// corners), and the Windows and Android sets expect full bleed. Only the four files macOS reads are taken
+// from the rounded rasterization; `icon.ico` and the iOS/Android sets stay as `tauri icon` drew them from
+// the square source.
+//
+// Usage: pnpm icons:macos
+
+import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';
+import { copyFileSync, mkdirSync, mkdtempSync, readFileSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
+import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
+import { dirname, join } from 'node:path';
+import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
+
+const root = join(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..');
+const assets = join(root, 'assets');
+const tauri = join(root, 'node_modules', '.bin', 'tauri');
+
+/** Source artwork paired with the `src-tauri` directory `bundle.icon` points at for that channel. */
+const CHANNELS = [
+  { source: 'icon.svg', icons: 'icons' },
+  { source: 'icon-purple.svg', icons: 'icons-preview' },
+  { source: 'icon-rust.svg', icons: 'icons-rust' },
+];
+
+/**
+ * The only files macOS reads: the `.icns` the bundle installs, plus the loose PNGs `bundle.icon` names.
+ * `icon.ico` is deliberately absent — Windows expects the square artwork.
+ */
+const MACOS_ICONS = ['32x32.png', '128x128.png', '128x128@2x.png', 'icon.icns'];
body:
Confirmed and fixed — the rounded output is now limited to `icon.icns` (the only file the macOS bundler reads); the `32x32`/`128x128`/`128x128@2x` PNGs are restored to the square artwork for Linux deb/AppImage, and the channel directory must now already exist rather than being created.

+---
+id: org.dxos.plugin.claudeAgents
+name: ClaudeAgentsPlugin
+version: 0.1.0
+---
+
+Models Anthropic Claude managed agents — agents Anthropic hosts and runs on your
+behalf — as objects in the space. A `ClaudeManagedAgent` holds the configuration
+(model, system prompt, toolsets, skills, MCP servers) and, once deployed, the
+server-assigned agent id. A `ClaudeAgentSession` records one run of that agent.
+
+Configuration and execution are deliberately separate: the object is edited
+locally and pushed to Anthropic by an explicit deploy step, so a half-configured
+agent never reaches the API. Session events are not mirrored into the space; the
+transcript is fetched on demand from the session id.
+
+## Extensions
+
+The following extension dialects are used in this document.
+Each extension is defined in the Appendix or resolved via its URI.
+
+| Term   | URI                            |
+|--------|--------------------------------|
+| `type` | `org.dxos.mdl.type@1.0`        |
+| `feat` | `org.dxos.mdl.feat@1.0`        |
+| `test` | `org.dxos.mdl.test@1.0`        |
body:
Not changing this one. The mismatch is the repo-wide `PLUGIN.mdl` template, not something introduced here: 73 `PLUGIN.mdl` files use the `org.dxos.mdl.*@1.0` table, and the 12 that carry the Appendix all pair it with `dxos.spec/ext/*@1.0` — including the file this one was modelled on. Diverging in a single plugin would make it the odd one out; if the scheme should be unified it wants a sweep across all of them, which is out of scope for this PR.

Correction to my last reply — I was wrong that migration is explicit. It is already automatic: `_anchorSpaceOnRootDocument` is wired to `stateUpdate` in `data-space-manager.ts:851` and runs on every path that opens a space. The reason the existing tests all call `migrateSpaceToRootDocument` by hand is the suppression at `data-space-manager.ts:509` — a space created legacy stays unanchored for the session that created it, so that there is a pre-migration state to migrate from.

So the transparent path was the untested one. Added in `244a4f75`:

`a legacy space anchors itself on the next load, with nobody calling migrate` — creates the space with `useSpaceRootDocument: false`, asserts it is unanchored, then restarts the manager (a fresh `DataSpaceManager` over the same stores, since the suppression lives on the instance and a plain close/open would still be the creating session), activates the lazily loaded space, and asserts it anchored with `idDerivation: 'spaceKey'` — no migrate call anywhere in the test.

That plus `796d4834` covers both halves of what you asked for: the migration happens on its own, and data written beforehand still resolves afterwards. No behaviour change was needed.

Real inconsistency, thanks — but resolved in the opposite direction, so flagging rather than silently closing.

You were comparing two sections that disagreed, and the one I've kept is the "one file" one. `#7`'s plan entry reads *"Re-point `protoMessage()` / `serviceError` at buf (64 sites, one file)"*, and that is achievable: `protoMessage(typeName)` now resolves the type in a buf registry and encodes through the shape-compat layer, which reproduces the protobuf.js field shapes. Callers cannot observe which codec carried a type, so no consumer changes.

The section you quoted was my own error — I'd conflated "re-point `protoMessage` at buf" with "move consumers to `bufMessage` types". The latter does rewrite every consumer, and it is the import sweep, priced separately. `49929a0b` replaces that section with what actually landed, measured: 31 of 46 types route through buf; the other 15 carry a transitive `google.protobuf.Any`, which shape-compat can't represent, so they stay on protobuf.js until `Any` support lands in `#3`.

Worth noting what that work surfaced, since it argues for the approach: shape-compat was double-encoding `google.protobuf.Struct`. `protoc-gen-es` already types a Struct field as a plain `JsonObject`, so re-encoding it produced a Struct keyed `fields` — 105 bytes against the legacy 43, and valid legacy bytes decoding to `{}`. `dxos.error.Error` carries the only Struct on the RPC error channel and `serviceError` rides every service call, so every RPC error's `context` would have silently emptied. Fixed with a regression test.

Not taking this one — the premise is inverted.

`Error` in `ModuleBody` isn't an untyped channel this code introduced; it's the framework's existing contract for *every* module, declared on `PluginModule.activate` itself (`plugin.ts:142-144`):

```ts
activate: (…) => Effect.Effect<ModuleActivateResult, Error, Capability.Service | Service | Scope.Scope | never>;
```

`ModuleBody` matches that signature deliberately, because a descriptor module's default export has to satisfy the same boundary a hand-written `addModule` body does. Narrowing it to a named error type would make descriptor-loaded modules *stricter* than every other module in the framework and would not typecheck against `PluginModule.activate` — the contract is what it is at the boundary, so the fix would have to change the framework-wide signature, which is well outside this PR.

The errors this code does own are typed: `PluginDescriptorError` with `load-failed`, `missing-default`, `decode-failed` and `relative-src-without-base` reasons, all raised through `Effect.tryPromise<ModuleBody<T>, PluginDescriptorError>` rather than left to escape.

## At a glance

- **Founded:** 2016
- **Location:** Roastery + cafe at 412 Linden Avenue, Oakland, CA. Small green-coffee warehouse next door.
- **Headcount:** 8 full-time, 4 part-time baristas.
- **Business mix:** ~60% wholesale (cafes, bakeries, small restaurants), ~30% retail (the cafe and a webshop), ~10% subscriptions.
- **Volume:** roughly 1,800 lbs roasted per week across all blends and single-origins.

## History

Bramble was founded by **Kai Chen** (head roaster) and **Diego Alvarez** (sourcing) after they spent four years together at a larger Bay Area roaster. They opened with a single 12 kg Loring roaster, three wholesale accounts, and a corner of a friend's bakery. They moved into the Linden Avenue space in 2019 and added the second roaster in 2022.

The name "Bramble" comes from the tangle of fruit notes Kai kept describing in the Ethiopian naturals she was cupping the day they wrote the business plan.

## Mission and voice

- **Mission:** Make specialty coffee that respects the farm at the front and the cafe at the back. Pay above market for green coffee, charge fair for roasted, keep the supply chain short enough to remember everyone's name.
- **Brand voice:** Warm, plainspoken, a little nerdy. We talk about coffee like it's food — terroir, ripeness, what the farmer was trying to do — not like it's wine and not like it's fuel. We don't use jargon when a normal word will do. We say please, thank you, and we send handwritten cards when a customer reorders for the fifth time.

## Product lines

| Line          | Examples                                                               | Notes                                       |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| Single-origin | Finca Esperanza (Colombia, washed), Sidamo Lot #42 (Ethiopia, natural) | Rotating; ~3 SKUs at any time.              |
| Blends        | Linden (everyday espresso), Field Notes (filter), Late Shift (dark)    | Year-round; Linden is the wholesale anchor. |
| Seasonal      | **Spring Blend** (in launch), Holiday Blend (Q4)                       | Two per year.                               |
| Decaf         | Swiss Water Colombia                                                   | One SKU.                                    |
| Retail        | 12 oz bags, gift boxes, brewing gear                                   | In the cafe and online.                     |

## Sourcing philosophy

- Direct trade where the relationship is real; transparent-trade through a small set of trusted importers otherwise.
- At least one origin visit per year per major lot.
- We pay floor prices above the C-market and above Fair Trade. We share lot-level pricing with wholesale partners on request.
- We prefer farms we've bought from for 2+ years over chasing one-off competition lots.

### Named partner farms / cooperatives

- **Finca Esperanza** — Huila, Colombia. Family farm run by **Carmen Restrepo**. We've bought from her since 2018. Washed caturra and pink bourbon. Q2 is harvest; Q3 is shipment.
- **Sidamo Cooperative** — Sidamo, Ethiopia. Contact **Abel Tadesse**, export liaison. Naturals; we usually buy lots #38–#45 each year.
- We also buy small parcels from Guatemala and Peru through importers; those are not named in this exemplar.

## Wholesale customers

- **North Star Café** — Portland, OR. Owner-buyer **Jordan Park**. On the Linden blend and rotating single-origin. Reorders every 3 weeks; uses our subscription program.
- **Hatch Bakery** — Brooklyn, NY. Buyer **Priya Shah**. Linden + Field Notes. Currently piloting a new espresso blend with us (see Spring Blend Launch).
- **Olive & Vine** — Austin, TX. Buyer **Mateo Ruiz**. New account; just sent first samples.

## The team

Bramble is small; everyone wears two hats.

- **Kai Chen** — co-founder, head roaster. Reads cupping forms in her sleep. Final say on roast curves.
- **Diego Alvarez** — co-founder, sourcing & green buyer. On the road one week a month during harvest seasons.
- **Sam Okafor** — wholesale lead. Owns the customer relationships and the Linden inventory.
- **Riley Tanaka** — operations & logistics. Pallets, freight, the QuickBooks login, the weird vendor portals.
- Plus four baristas (rotating) and two part-time roastery assistants. Not individually named in the exemplar.

## Active initiatives

### Spring Blend Launch (current focus)

A new seasonal espresso blend targeting wholesale espresso bars. Going live in 6 weeks.

- Diego is locking in the green: lot from Finca Esperanza + a smaller Guatemalan parcel.
- Kai is iterating on the roast curve; current draft is two weeks old.
- Sam is coordinating cuppings with North Star, Hatch, and Olive & Vine.
- Riley is sorting packaging (label redesign with a freelancer) and freight.

### Q2 sourcing trip

Diego flies to Colombia → Ethiopia in five weeks. Two weeks total. He'll visit Finca Esperanza and the Sidamo cooperative, and meet a new Peruvian producer recommended by an importer.

## Conventions used in the exemplar data

When extending the exemplar, please keep these consistent:

- **Email addresses:** `firstname@bramblecoffee.com` for internal, organization-specific domains for partners (e.g. `carmen@fincaesperanza.co`, `abel@sidamocoop.org`, `jordan@northstarcafe.com`, `priya@hatchbakery.com`, `mateo@oliveandvine.cafe`).
- **Dates:** Recent emails should be spread across the last ~6 weeks. Calendar events span 2 weeks past → 2 weeks future. Hard-code ISO dates relative to the snapshot generation date; set the `NOW` env var (e.g. `NOW=2026-05-20`) for reproducible regeneration.
- **Tone in emails:** Plain, professional but warm. Use first names. No marketing fluff. Suppliers occasionally drop a Spanish or Amharic phrase (sparingly, accurately).
- **Locations and coordinates:** Use real coordinates so the Map view looks right. Oakland HQ, Portland (North Star), Brooklyn (Hatch), Austin (Olive & Vine), Huila Colombia (Finca Esperanza), Sidamo Ethiopia (Sidamo Cooperative).
- **No real-world business names** — every entity in this exemplar is fictional and should stay that way. Don't reuse the names of actual specialty roasters or cafes.

## Profile

- **Fragrance/Aroma:** Stone fruit, jasmine, light cocoa.
- **Acidity:** Bright, malic, well-structured.
- **Body:** Medium, silky.
- **Flavor:** Red apple, raspberry, milk chocolate, almond finish.
- **Aftertaste:** Long, clean, slightly floral.

Project: ![Spring Blend Launch](echo:///01M0RF1EWZM3C8J8PGZYS6MEYB)

## Setup

- Prepare 4 samples per session: v1, v2, v3, and the control (current Linden blend).
- Grind 10 g per sample, 200 ml at 94 °C.
- Evaluate dry fragrance, wet aroma, and taste at 4-min, 8-min, 12-min intervals.

## Brew parameters

1. **Espresso:** 18 g in / 36 g out / 27–30 s.
2. **Filter:** 1:16 ratio, 4:00 total time.

## Scoring dimensions

Fragrance/Aroma · Flavour · Aftertaste · Acidity · Body · Balance · Uniformity · Cleanliness · Sweetness

## Key targets

- Espresso-forward: good body at 1:2.5 ratio.
- Profile: fruit-forward (berry, stone fruit), chocolate mid, clean finish.
- Score on the SCA form, then add a short qualitative note.
- Re-cup after 7 days to check for stale Confirmed, but fixed differently — the suggested remedy isn't reachable from here.

The collision is real: `JsonSchema.toJsonSchema(Schema.Void)` and `…(Schema.Null)` both produce `{"type":"null"}`, so a routine declaring `null` takes the undeclared branch.

An explicit flag can't be propagated, though, because the distinction is already gone before this function sees anything: `Instructions.make` does `output ?? Schema.Void` and persists only the serialized schema, so nothing downstream can tell a defaulted output from a declared one — and objects already in spaces carry no flag to read. Carrying it would mean a new field on the `Instructions` schema.

Not worth that here: a routine whose declared output is `null` has no payload to validate, so both cases genuinely want the same tool. What changed instead — the sentinel's `type` is now read without the `as { type?: unknown }` cast (which the repo's no-cast rule disallows anyway), the conflation is documented on `isUndeclaredOutput` rather than left implicit, and a test asserts it so the behaviour is chosen rather than incidental.

body:
Both of the outside-diff findings from the latest review were real and are fixed in 93486651 — recording them here since they have no thread of their own.

**1. Eviction skipped a collected core's document.** `_evictRemovedObjects` filtered removals by `_objects.has(objectId)`, so a core collected *before* its directory entry was removed skipped release entirely: the document stayed bound, and `_rehydrateCore` could resurrect an object the directory no longer lists. That is the worse half — not a leak but a resurrection. The predicate now counts a bound document as much as a live core.

**2. An unsettled request was never dropped.** Release left a still-resolving satisfaction request in `_satisfactionRequests` / `_satisfactionSubscriptions` on the theory that "the object's next release will get it" — wrong, because the finalizer that reported the release fires exactly once. It is now dropped when it settles: deferred by a turn (aborting from inside the request's own state change would cancel the IO of ops whose refcount drops, which is the failure I chased earlier in this PR), and skipped if the object was re-acquired in the meantime.

Also in that commit: the CI break was mine — `object-release.test.ts` asserted identity via `_loadObjectById`, which is internal to `DatabaseImpl` and not on `EchoDatabase`. `moon run …:test` transpiles without typechecking, so only `:build` caught it; it now compares two query passes, which is the public route to the same invariant. And the flagged comments are trimmed to one clause each.

Verified: `echo-client-e2e:test` 319 passed, `echo-client:test` 534 passed, both `:build` targets typecheck, lints clean, and each retention test passes standalone from a clean `wasm 5.2MB` floor.

Skipping this one deliberately — stripping the prefix would make the compat layer diverge from the codec it exists to reproduce, and in the one place that is unsafe.

The premise about `Registry.getMessage` needing the exact name is right, but the legacy codec behaves the same way and that is the contract here:

- `ProtoCodec.encodeAsAny` writes `this._type.fullName.slice(1)` — the bare fully-qualified name. Nothing in dxos ever writes a prefixed `type_url`, so the case can only arrive from a foreign producer.
- On decode, `anySubstitutions` gates on `schema.hasType(value.type_url)`, which resolves through `tryGetCodecForType` and so fails on a prefixed URL exactly as `getMessage` does. Legacy leaves such a payload packed, and so does this layer.

So the finding is that we could be *more* permissive than the codec we're replacing. That is a shape change, and it lands on `Credential.subject.assertion` — the only `Any` reachable in practice. `getCredentialProofPayload` signs the canonical stringification of the decoded object, so flipping a payload from packed (`{'@type': 'google.protobuf.Any', type_url, value}`) to resolved changes the signed bytes and would fail verification for any credential carrying a prefixed URL. Byte-for-byte parity with the legacy shapes is what makes the rest of this migration safe to land incrementally.

Worth revisiting when something buf-native starts packing with `anyPack`, which does emit `type.googleapis.com/…` — at that point the right fix is a prefix-normalising step on the *producer* side, not a more permissive resolver on the consumer side. I've not added it here.

The other four comments are addressed in `4b25ecb`: one changeset entry (both packages are in the same fixed group — correct catch), `expect` from the test context, the helper moved below the suite, and the over-long comments trimmed to one clause each. That last one also turned up a wrong pointer — a comment named `signing.test.ts` where the assertions actually live in `buf-compat.test.ts` — now corrected.

+## The `preserveAny` caller option, and what it unblocked
+
+`anySubstitutions` preserves an `Any` when **either** the field carries `[(preserve_any) = true]` **or**

+which silently excluded the two production sites relying on the caller half -- neither `dxos/rpc.proto`
+nor `dxos/mesh/messaging.proto` marks its `Any` fields, so the option is the only thing keeping those
+payloads packed:

+| Site                              | Message                               | Why it stays packed                                                                        |
+| --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
+| `mesh/rpc/src/rpc.ts`             | `dxos.rpc.RpcMessage`                 | Frames every RPC between peers; the payload is the callee's business, not the transport's. |
+| `mesh/messaging/src/messenger.ts` | `dxos.mesh.messaging.ReliablePayload` | Rides the signalling network; the peer resolves it, not the relay.                         |

+on the compat codec. These are the highest-traffic wire formats in the repo -- a byte mismatch breaks

Correct, and thanks — that sentence was stale. I wrote "both carry byte-equality fixtures" before discovering the `stream: false` divergence, then changed the `RpcMessage` fixture to cross-codec round-trips and never updated the prose. Fixed in `0bff3bcf`, split explicitly rather than softened:

body:
Not doing this one — routing these two through `@dxos/config` would break what both modules exist to guarantee.

`cors-proxy.ts` and `service/edge-service.ts` (which `Image.ts` builds on) each carry a header saying they are deliberately free of heavy `@dxos` dependencies so they bundle into workerd and the browser — `cors-proxy.ts` names protobufjs specifically, `edge-service.ts` states its only runtime deps are `effect` and `@dxos/log`.

`@dxos/config` is not a light import: it pulls `@dxos/protocols` (protobuf) and `@dxos/client-protocol`, which brings `@dxos/echo`, `@dxos/echo-client`, `@dxos/credentials` and `@dxos/rpc`. `edge-client` does not currently depend on `@dxos/config` at all, so this would be a new package edge. Concretely relevant here: this PR is already 521 bytes over the `boot-budget` ceiling, and `@dxos/config` is boot-reachable while that dependency edge is not.

The overlap is also narrower than it looks. `DEFAULT_IMAGE_SERVICE_URL` and `LEGACY_CORS_PROXY_URL` are last-resort fallbacks for callers that pass no base URL; every caller that *has* config already resolves through `getEdgeServiceEndpoint` and passes the result in — `plugin-crm/attach-image.ts` and `plugin-support/screenshot.ts` both do, via `EDGE_SERVICE_DEFAULTS[EdgeServiceName.Image]`. So `runtime.services.edgeServices` overrides are honoured on the paths that can honour them; these constants only cover the case where there is no config to consult.

Worth revisiting if `EdgeServiceClient` ever grows a config-aware constructor in a package that may depend on `@dxos/config` — then the fallback can move there and these two literals go away.

Done in 79151cc7 — `readonly input: Schema.Codec<_Input, any>` / `readonly output: Schema.Codec<_Output, any>`.

Worth noting what it caught: `AgentService` restated the agent handle's input as `string | ContentBlock.Any[]`, but `AgentProcess`'s schema is `Schema.Union([Schema.String, Schema.Array(ContentBlock.Any)])`, whose Type has a **readonly** array. `Codec<any, any>` erased that, so the hand-written type had silently drifted from the schema; with the parameters in place it stopped compiling. `AgentHandle` is now derived from the definition instead of restated:

```ts
type AgentHandle =
  ReturnType<typeof AgentProcess> extends Process.Process<infer Input, infer Output, any, infer Rpcs>
    ? ProcessManager.Handle<Input, Output, Rpcs>
    : never;
```

so input, output and the RPC group all come from one place and can't drift again. `compute` 73 passed, `compute-runtime` 169 passed / 1 skipped, `agent-runtime` 30 passed / 21 skipped.

The encoded side stays `any` deliberately — nothing here depends on the wire type, and pinning it would mean threading a third parameter through `Process` for no consumer.

Real finding, fixed in df60955 — but the opposite way round from the suggestion, so noting the divergence.

Binding it in `given` would be wrong: `given` states preconditions that hold *before* the flow runs, and this connection does not exist until step 6 creates it. The other route, `capture`, only names an `invoke`'s result — and step 6 has no `invoke`, because creating the connection is a UI gesture through the credential dialog with no operation behind it. So there was nothing legitimate for `$given.connection` to point at, which is why the reference dangled in the first place.

The teardown is now human-only like every other step in this `actors: human` flow: click "Delete connection" in the connection's own panel, which routes through `space.removeObjects` itself — so cleanup still happens, and that is what the recording actually did. A `note` records why there is no binding.

If this flow later gains an agent path, the fix is a create operation for the connection; step 6 could then `capture` it and the teardown could `invoke` against that.

The lease proxies what callers actually used: `doc()`, `heads()`, `change()`, `changeAt()`, `waitUntilReady()`, `on`/`off`/`once`, `subscribe()`, plus `state`, `url` and `documentId`. Two notes on the surface:

- `url` is derived from the id, so it still reads after disposal — the same reasoning as `documentId`: an id names a document, it does not claim one.

body:
Real, and fixed in `c4d2ac6c`.

`evict` now reports whether the document was actually unloaded — `_evictDocument` returns `false` when it declines one that never settled — and the registry requeues it instead of dropping it from `#idle`. Two details the requeue needs:

- **Re-stamped rather than restored to its old position.** Keeping the original `releasedAt` would make `#scheduleDrain` compute a zero wait and retry in a tight loop against a document that is still loading. Re-stamping spaces each retry by the idle delay; strict release order is the thing given up, deliberately.
- **One attempt per drain**, tracked in a local set that `#evictable` skips, so a forced drain — which ignores the delay — cannot spin on an unevictable document either.

A rejected eviction lands in the same requeue (the `catch` leaves `evicted` false). A cancelled one does not: `isCancelled()` means a lease exists again, so the count check re-opens the document rather than requeuing it.

Took the `subscribe` finding too — a real hole in hiding the handle, since `QueryState`'s ready variant carries it. It now passes `{ state }` only.

Fixed — the handle is stored and released in `_close`. `FunctionContext` is a `Resource`, so a reopen would otherwise have stacked a second registration on the same graph.

_🤖 Addressed by [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)_

author: richburdon
body:
Fixed — added `S3TimeoutError`, raised only when our own deadline fired, so a slow endpoint no longer tells the user to fix a bucket policy that is already correct.

_🤖 Addressed by [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)_

author: richburdon
body:
Fixed, though not with a per-space allowlist. Private, loopback and metadata hosts are rejected in `toHttpsUrl` before any request is built, using the same guard `plugin-crm` uses — that closes the reachable exposure (an internal address via the unsigned read path) without a new per-space registry to keep in sync. An allowlist would additionally constrain *public* endpoints, which is a stricter policy worth deciding separately. Bracketed IPv6 needed its own port handling; tests cover it.

_🤖 Addressed by [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)_

author: richburdon
body:
Both bypasses fixed. Redirects are now refused (`redirect: 'error'`, plus a guard for a proxied 3xx) rather than followed to a host nobody validated. The hex spelling of IPv4-mapped IPv6 is now unwrapped too — `::ffff:7f00:1` was reaching the same address as 127.0.0.1 past the dotted-quad check. Tests cover the hex form of loopback, metadata and private addresses, and the redirect refusal. Not done: resolved-peer-IP validation via an egress component, which needs infrastructure this PR does not have — worth raising separately.

_🤖 Addressed by [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)_

author: richburdon
body:
Fixed — the cap is now applied to the encoded length before `atob`, so an oversized payload is rejected without materialising the buffer. The post-decode check stays as a backstop.

_🤖 Addressed by [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)_

author: richburdon
body:
Fixed — `isAcceptedMimeType` now trims and lowercases before comparing, so `Text/Plain` is accepted. RFC 2045 makes type and subtype case-insensitive, and a server is within its rights to answer that way.

_🤖 Addressed by [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)_

author: richburdon
body:
Fixed in 0b42396. `request()` now returns a `read` wrapper alongside `response`/`done`; body reads go through it, and it re-throws `S3TimeoutError` when the `timedOut` flag is set, so an abort during the body phase is classified the same way as one during the header phase. Threaded through `probeAccess`, `putObject`, `getObject` and `headObject`.

The timeout branch itself is not covered by a test — a fake-timer version did not reliably intercept the already-scheduled timer and hung on the real 15s deadline. There is a test for the other half (a non-timeout body-read failure passes through unrelabelled), and the gap is documented in a comment above it rather than papered over.

_🤖 Addressed by [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)_

author: richburdon
body:
Fixed in 0b42396. `toHttpsUrl` now builds the `URL` first and validates the *parsed* authority — `url.username`/`url.password` are rejected outright, and `isBlockedHost` runs against `url.hostname`, which is what `fetch` actually connects to. Regression test added covering both `bucket.s3.amazonaws.com:443@169.254.169.254` and `user:pass@127.0.0.1`. The old string-based `hostnameOf` helper is gone.

_🤖 Addressed by [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)_

author: richburdon
body:
Fixed in 0b42396. The input is keyed on the stored name (`key={name ?? ""}`), so a replicated rename remounts it and the field picks up the new value instead of holding stale text that the next blur would write back.

_🤖 Addressed by [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)_

author: richburdon
body:
Skipping — a tagged error would be inconsistent here and buys nothing.

The contract is `onValidate?: (...) => Effect.Effect<void, Error>` (`plugin-connector/src/types/ConnectorSpec.ts:214`), and both consumers (`CreateConnectionPanel` and `CustomTokenDialog`) do the same thing with the failure: read `.message` and put it in the inline error span. There is no branch that discriminates on a tag.

Every other connector in the repo does it the same way — `plugin-discord`, `plugin-deepseek`, `plugin-jmap` all `Effect.fail(new Error(...))` in `onValidate`. Introducing a tagged error in `plugin-s3` alone would make it the odd one out without changing behaviour. If the contract is ever narrowed to a tagged type, that is a `plugin-connector` change that should convert all five connectors at once, not just this one.

_🤖 Addressed by [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)_

author: richburdon
body:
Valid, fixed in 21856b18 — took the first option, clearing `lastFingerprint` before the flush.

The watcher event is better evidence than the fingerprint: it says the file changed, whereas mtime plus size can both survive an edit (a same-length change written inside the same millisecond). Skipping there was the worst outcome of the three, since `rebuild` would still send the full reload and the page would come back showing the old sprite.

Preferred it over a content digest to keep the common path cheap — the fingerprint is computed on every write attempt across every resolved symbol, so hashing file contents there would cost far more than the one case it fixes.

body:
Valid, fixed in 056e010a. Took the second suggestion — classify every non-inheriting paint value — rather than adding named colors, since CSS has ~150 of them and an allowlist of the inheriting values cannot miss one:

```ts
const INHERITING = new Set(["currentcolor", "none", "inherit", "initial", "revert", "revert-layer", "transparent", "unset", "context-fill", "context-stroke"]);
```

Anything else is reported. `var()` is deliberately allowed through: its value is unknowable at build time and flagging it would be noise.

This also caught a case neither of us named — paint set as an *attribute* rather than in a `style` (`<path fill="red">`), which overrides the symbol fill just the same.

Added your `stroke:red` case plus 10 more (`rebeccapurple`, `rgb()`, `url(#gradient)`, and negatives for `transparent`, `var()`, `fill-rule`, `stroke-width`, `stroke-linecap`). Also ran it against the real set to check for false positives — no warnings, since the current assets only declare `fill-rule` and `stroke-width`, which are not paint properties.

Done in 9fede9f — `findSession` is gone; the processor calls `getSession` on both paths through one `#getSession()` helper.

One consequence worth naming: `getSession` spawns when there is no process, so a mounted chat now spawns its agent process up front instead of on first prompt (it parks in `IDLE`, and `running` stays `false`, so nothing else changes). Confirmed and fixed in 9d4b6159 — this was a real defect, thanks.

`resolveTasks` filters on `ref.isAvailable`, so an unloaded sub-task was invisible to `Task.subtree`, stayed in `chat.tasks`, and was never passed to `db.remove`. With every member parented to the chat, the cascade could not reach it either, so it ended up with a dangling `parentTask` — which `Task.rootTasks` reads as a root, exactly as you describe.

Rather than traverse by ref id (a child's `parentTask` lives on the child, so descending genuinely needs the children loaded), the loaded checklist is now an explicit parameter:

```ts
export const deleteTask = (db, chat, tasks: readonly Task.Task[], task: Task.Task): Task.Task[]
```

That puts the requirement at the call site instead of leaving it implicit, matching the shape main's #12816 gave `collectSubtree`. The slash commands hydrate once up front, which also fixes the selector case from your out-of-diff comment: an unresolved entry could make a valid ordinal or exact title report "no matching task".

Added the coverage you asked for — `deleteTask sweeps a sub-task whose ref was never resolved` asserts `Chat.resolveTasks` sees both tasks, then that deleting the parent empties `chat.tasks` and returns both ids.

Confirmed and fixed in 3b778372. `RefImpl.load()` throws `Object not found` at `ref.ts:567`, so one dangling entry rejected the whole `Promise.all` and took the command with it — a regression `hydrate` introduced, since the previous `Chat.resolveTasks`-only path never threw.

Used `ref.tryLoad()` rather than a per-ref catch: it's the tolerant variant the ECHO API already provides, and it matches how `Chat.loadTasks` and `TaskSet.loadTasks` skip a dangling ref via `Effect.orElseSucceed`. Narrower than catching by message, too — no string matching on `'Object not found'`, and any other failure still propagates.

Reproduced before fixing. The new test removes a task behind the array's back, then runs `/task:delete 1`:

- against `load()` → `× a dangling checklist entry does not fail the command`, `Error: Object not found`
- against `tryLoad()` → 6/6 pass

body:
You're right, and thanks — my assertion `expect(Chat.resolveTasks(chat)).toHaveLength(2)` proved the child *was* resolved, so the test contradicted its own name. Replaced in 3b778372.

I could not do quite what you suggested. `isAvailable` is `#target !== undefined || #resolver !== undefined` (`ref.ts:549`), so a db-backed ref is "available" whenever a resolver is attached — the omission from `resolveTasks` comes from `.target` being `undefined` for an object outside the working set, which `dedupeById` then drops. Producing that in-process would need working-set eviction or a reopen, and this suite runs on `AssistantTestLayer` with a single live database. A resolver-less ref isn't a substitute either: `load`/`tryLoad` assert on `#resolver`, so `Chat.loadTasks` could not restore it, and the test would assert the wrong mechanism.

So the test now asserts the contract directly, which is the part that actually protects the caller:

- `Chat.deleteTask(db, chat, [parent], parent)` — a partial list, exactly what the sync reader yields when a child is outside the working set — returns only the parent and leaves the child's ref in `chat.tasks`.
- Passing `yield* Chat.loadTasks(chat)` takes parent and child together and empties the array.

That documents why the parameter exists and fails if the sweep regresses, without pretending to construct a state this harness can't reach. The stronger coverage of the load path is in `plugin-assistant` — `a dangling checklist entry does not fail the command` — which does exercise real unresolvable refs and fails against `ref.load()`.

Confirmed and fixed in `98f4a5c6`.

Measured it against the legacy codec before changing anything, on a `Claim` whose `assertion` carries an `AuthenticateRequest` (a registered type with a raw `bytes` field), decoded from a `Buffer` input:

```
legacy nested challenge: Buffer
compat nested challenge: Uint8Array
```

So this was the same defect as the parent commit, one level down: `391d06c6` stopped flattening `bytes` at the top level, but `anyFromProto` still ran the payload through `toWireBytes` before the nested `decodeCompat`, and since `BinaryReader.bytes()` returns a subarray of the buffer it was handed, every byte field inside the payload was a view over that flattened copy. It matters because a credential's signature reaches its verifier through this path.

`toWireBytes` is gone from the decode side; encoding still flattens, since buf accepts any view on the way in.

Added `bytes inside a resolved Any payload keep the input's view type`, which asserts the nested field is a `Buffer` for both codecs rather than only comparing bytes — the pre-existing assertions compare through `canonicalStringify`, which renders a `Buffer` and a `Uint8Array` identically and so could not see either level of this.

Verified: protocols 52, `shell:test-browser` 10 passed, plus codec-protobuf, rpc, credentials, echo-host, client-services, client, teleport and network-manager — 78 tasks, exit 0.
