Real bug, confirmed and fixed in 715b001e — pushed ahead of auto-merge, since this would otherwise have landed.

Reproduced before fixing:

```
aKeys [ 'a' ] bKeys [ 'b' ] sameLen true
every Object.is => true      // reported equal
```

Used `Object.hasOwn` rather than `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call` — same semantics, and the codebase targets a runtime that has it.

Two regression tests, both verified to fail without the fix and pass with it:

```
× differing key names with undefined values
× a key present on one side only, holding undefined
   Tests  2 failed | 10 passed (12)     ← fix reverted
   Tests  134 passed | 1 skipped (135)  ← fix applied
```

Worth being explicit about the blast radius, because it is wider than the array bug you caught earlier. `shallowEqual` now backs three call sites: `Surface`'s subtree re-render decision, `app-graph`'s node-change detection, and `schema`'s `StateMap`. A rename between two absent-valued keys was invisible to all three — a node whose data went from `{ a: undefined }` to `{ b: undefined }` read as unchanged.

Consumers re-run after the fix:

```
util           134 passed
app-graph      128 passed
schema          51 passed
app-framework  267 passed
```

On the accompanying nit about moving `StablePlugin` / `mountStableHost` below the closing `describe` — not doing that one, for the reason I gave when it came up before. The guideline is *"Place test layer, configuration, and main definitions at the top of the suite; helpers at the bottom"*, and these are plugin definitions, not helpers. All six sibling plugin definitions in this file (`TestPlugin`, `MappedPropsPlugin`, `InvalidIdPlugin`, `GatedPlugin`, …) sit at module scope immediately above the describe that consumes them, and `probe` — an actual helper — is up there too. Moving these two 500 lines from their only call site would make the file less consistent, not more.

+```mdl
+rule declare-optional-services-with-noop-layers: An optional service is a declared requirement plus a noop layer, never a callback
+  A layer that needs a service only sometimes must still DECLARE it — in the
+  `Layer` signature's requirements, and in a `LayerSpec`'s `requires` — and the
+  hosts that lack a real implementation must satisfy it with a documented noop
+  layer (`layerNoop`). Do not reach for the alternatives: an
+  `Effect.serviceOption` read is invisible to a `LayerSpec` stack, where a tag
+  the spec does not require is never in its context, so the read comes back
+  empty even when the app materialises the service elsewhere; and a
+  `getFooManager?: () => Effect<Foo>` callback option moves the wiring out of
+  the layer graph into a caller that has to re-derive it, so the graph no longer
+  tells you what the layer needs and each host wires it differently — or
+  forgets to. The usual justification for both is that requiring the tag would
+  prune the provider on a host that does not use the feature; a noop layer
+  answers that directly, and fails loudly at the point of use rather than
+  silently disabling the feature at construction. Flag an
+  `Effect.serviceOption` whose tag is not in the enclosing layer's
+  requirements, a `LayerSpec` factory reading a tag absent from its `requires`,
+  and an options field typed as a thunk returning a service or an `Effect` of
+  one. `Effect.serviceOption` for a genuinely optional *value* (a config
+  default, a capability list that may be empty) is NOT a violation, and neither
+  is a callback that supplies behaviour rather than a service — a strategy, a
+  factory the host parameterises.
+  scope: repo
+  files:
+    - packages/**/*.ts
+  grep: serviceOption|LayerSpec|get[A-Z]\w*(Manager|Service|Provider)\?:

Fixed in f69dded0, though not with the proposed regex — `\w+\?:.*=>:` has a trailing colon that makes it match nothing.

The pre-filter is now `serviceOption|LayerSpec|\w+\?:.*=>.*(Service|Manager|Provider|Layer)\b`: syntax-based on the optional-arrow-field shape, but still requiring the type to name a service, so it catches `aiServiceMiddleware?: (aiService: AiService.Service) => AiService.Service` and `getProcessManager?: () => ProcessManager` without pulling in every `onChange?: (value: string) => void` in the repo. Behaviour-callback exclusion stays in the rule prose, as you suggest.

+## Phase 8 — the model round trip (session of 2026-09-08)
+
+The one remaining item from Phase 5's `resume` ("the agent model round trip needs the memoized
+Anthropic fixture") turned out to sit behind FIVE defects, each hiding the next. Diagnosed against a
+new round-trip test rather than by reading: every hypothesis reached from source alone was wrong.
+
+### Runtime defects fixed (dxos, commit c78bea1b12 + working tree)
+
+- [x] **`RemoteProcessManager` is a required dependency of `AgentService.layer`**, not an optional
+      read. A `LayerSpec` stack never has a tag its spec does not require in context, so
+      `Effect.serviceOption` always came back empty and every `location: 'edge'` session failed with
+      "no RemoteProcessManager is available" while the app had materialised one all along. Hosts
+      without EDGE satisfy it with `RemoteProcessManager.layerNoop`.
+- [x] **`EdgeProcessManager.fromClient` supplies the process-control surface.** It was cancel-only,
+      deferring to a `forSpace` that exists nowhere in the repo, so the manager an app builds lacked
+      `spawn`/`list` entirely ("offers no process control").
+- [x] **A `Process` definition declares the schemas its data model needs** (`Process.types`), and the
+      host registers them with the process's database. `FunctionContext._open` does the registering;
+      passing `types` to the constructor alone was inert, which cost a full cycle to notice.
+      `SessionStore` reads the conversation with a TYPED query, so on a host that registered nothing
+      the agent appended a prompt and read the queue back empty — a lost write, in appearance.
+- [x] **A fresh agent no longer completes on its first empty-queue wake** (`turnRan`). `onSpawn`
+      discards what it inherits, so a new process always starts empty; treating that as "work
+      drained" ended the agent ~50ms after spawn, and the prompt it was spawned for then landed on a
+      finished handle and was dropped with a warning.
+- [x] **Read-your-writes over an eventually-consistent queue read.** A hosted process's feed read is
+      served by the space INDEX: the agent appends a prompt and its own read, 11ms later, returns
+      empty; the index catches up ~3ms after that, but the agent has already gone idle and nothing
+      looks again. `onAlarm` now re-arms a short alarm while a write it made is unread (bounded by
+      `MAX_UNSEEN_WRITE_WAKES`), instead of concluding the queue is drained. Locally this never
+      reproduces — the same read is served from the resident feed handle.
+

+14:38:25.657 agent onAlarm handling {"tag":"message","id":"01M20Q9AQ2ASCTPA9N56TZKDNM"}
+14:38:29.126 agent onAlarm handling {"tag":"message","id":"01M20Q9AQ2ASCTPA9N56TZKDNM"}   (×5)

+      would replace this mechanism rather than extend it.
body:
Fixed on the current head — the TASKS.md lines you quoted were the record of the bug, not a decision to ship with it.

The ack loop is closed by durable suppression, as you propose: an `ackedEntries` `StorageService.cell` records each entry id at ack time, the pending-selection filters those ids out, and ids no longer pending are pruned from the cell so it does not grow without bound. That makes the suppression survive hibernation rather than living in the incarnation's memory. The second-turn and completion tests pass against it (`agent-runtime` 45 passed, and the edge harness's multi-turn case).

Real, and fixed in ec798dc4. Reproduced first:

```
DX_REACT_COMPILER=0     -> true
DX_REACT_COMPILER=false -> true
```

Both sites now use an allowlist rather than a new parser, because this file already has the idiom for exactly this case a few hundred lines down:

```ts
...(['1', 'true'].includes(process.env.DX_RUN_MANUAL_TESTS ?? '') ? [] : ['manual']),
```

So `REACT_COMPILER_ALL` and the storybook builder both became `['1', 'true'].includes(process.env.DX_REACT_COMPILER ?? '')`, with a comment at each site saying why, so it doesn't get "simplified" back to `!!` later.

One deliberate departure from your suggestion: you asked for "the same parsed flag" in both places, which reads as export-and-import. I repeated the one-line idiom instead. `tools/storybook-react/.storybook/main.ts` imports no root config today, and pulling in `vite.base.config.ts` for a single boolean would drag its module-level evaluation (profile dirs, plugin construction) into storybook's config load. A shared helper is worth it when the logic is non-trivial; here it is one `includes` call that already appears verbatim in the repo.

Behaviour, matching `DX_RUN_MANUAL_TESTS` exactly:

```
"1" -> true     "0"     -> false
"true" -> true  "false" -> false
                ""      -> false
                unset   -> false
                "yes"   -> false
                "TRUE"  -> false
```

`TRUE` staying false is inherited from the existing idiom rather than intended — I kept the semantics identical instead of quietly making this one flag more permissive than its neighbour. Documented usage is `=1`.

`oxfmt` reports both files already formatted; CI covers the rest.

Worth noting for whoever touches it next: `DEBUG_LEAKS = !!process.env.DX_DEBUG_LEAKS` at line 77 has the same shape. I have not changed it — it is unrelated to this PR, and the consequence there (heap snapshots) is far less surprising than silently enabling an experimental compiler.

+# `@dxos/react-ui-form` — Design
+
+Schema-driven forms. Give `Form.Root` an Effect `schema` and `values`; a field set renders typed
+controls for every property. Hand-written rows and groups use the same parts, with or without a
+binding to the model.
+
+## Ontology
+
+Three fixed points: `Form.Root` is the outer scope, with or without a schema, and forms nest; the
+leaves are fields; fields are grouped by field sets, which carry their own label. Three concerns are
+kept apart and never decide each other:
+
+1. **Binding** — where a value and its validation status come from: the form model at a `path`,
+   or state the caller owns.
+2. **Semantics** — the label, helper-text and error-text association: Ark's `Field` and
+   `Fieldset`, wrapped by `@dxos/react-ui`.
+3. **Layout** — the card grid, the presentation modes, the required mark, the depth chrome.
+
+A row or group is **bound** when it has a `path` (or sits under a `Form.Root path`) and its parts
+read the binding through one hook, `useFormField`; without a path it is **unbound** and the caller
+wires the control. Nothing in how the row renders differs between the two. Decided 2026-09-08:
+`Form.Field` and `Form.FieldSet` are what a consumer writes in every case, so this package owns the
+row and the group and `@dxos/react-ui`'s `Field`/`Fieldset` stay primitives, with the names mapping
+one for one: `Form.Field` is a `Field`, `Form.FieldSet` is a `Fieldset`. Walking the schema is a
+third part, `Form.Fields`, which renders no element, so no component's behaviour depends on whether
+it was given children. A form built by hand is `Form.FieldSet`s of `Form.Field`s and never mentions
+`Form.Fields`; the walker appears only where the schema should supply the fields, and a mixed form
+uses both inside one field set. `Form.Root` is the only path scope besides `Form.Field` itself.
body:
Stated as suggested: `Form.Root` is the only component that scopes descendant context; `Form.Field`, `Form.Fields` and `Form.List` take a `path` for their own binding or enumeration, written from the enclosing root, and `Form.Root path` re-roots only to embed a component written against a sub-schema.

+one for one: `Form.Field` is a `Field`, `Form.FieldSet` is a `Fieldset`. Walking the schema is a
+third part, `Form.Fields`, which renders no element, so no component's behaviour depends on whether
+it was given children. A form built by hand is `Form.FieldSet`s of `Form.Field`s and never mentions
+`Form.Fields`; the walker appears only where the schema should supply the fields, and a mixed form
+uses both inside one field set. `Form.Root` is the only path scope besides `Form.Field` itself.
+
+| Component        | Built from                                                                                  | Role                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
+| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
+| `Form.Root`      | nothing (a scope; only the outermost with `onSave` renders `<form>`)                        | The model boundary: `schema?`, `values`/`defaultValues`, `onValuesChanged`, `onSave`, `autoSave`, and the modes as context (`readonly`, `presentation`, `variant`). Nests two ways: with `path` it binds a sub-tree of the enclosing model and shares its validation, which is also how hand-placed fields of a nested object are scoped; with its own `schema` + `values` it is an independent form embedded in another. |
+| `Form.Viewport`  | `ScrollArea`                                                                                | The scroll region.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
+| `Form.Content`   | nothing                                                                                     | The measure and gutter inside the viewport: the bounded surface the scroll region lives in, as Popover's `Content` is to its `Viewport`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
+| `Form.FieldSet`  | `Fieldset.Root` + `Legend` + `HelperText` + `ErrorText`; `Collapsible.*` when `collapsible` | Presentation and semantics only: `label`, `description`, `collapsible`, `bordered`, with depth chrome from context (a top-level legend is a heading with the section gap, a nested one a plain legend with an indented body). Wraps anything: fields, walkers, other field sets, hand-written rows. No `path`, no enumeration.                                                                                            |
+| `Form.Fields`    | nothing                                                                                     | The walker: `path?`, `include`, `exclude`, `sort`, `filter`, resolved against the enclosing scope. Renders a `Form.Field` per property and, for a nested object, a `Form.FieldSet` (label from the schema title, collapsible) around a `Form.Fields` at that path.                                                                                                                                                        |
+| `Form.Field`     | `Field.Root` + `Label` + `HelperText` + `ErrorText` + the control                           | The leaf, always a real field. With `path` it is bound: label, description, value, error, required and readonly come from the schema and model, and with no children the dispatcher picks the control. Without `path` it takes `label`/`description`/`error` as props and its children are the control. `standalone` for a row with no single control (a button, a readout).                                              |
+| `Form.List`      | `Fieldset.Root` + `Legend`; items are `Form.FieldSet` / `Form.Field`                        | The repeating group (an array property): `path`, an item template, `Form.List.Item` with move and remove, `Form.List.Add`. Ark has no repeater; this is the one form-specific structure.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
+| `Form.Layout`    | nothing                                                                                     | Visual arrangement with no semantics: columns, inline pairs, the parsed layout spec. Used inside a field set, never in place of one.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
+| `Form.Actions`   | nothing (`Dialog.ActionBar` is the sibling)                                                 | The action row: `Form.Submit`, `Form.Cancel`, `Form.Reset`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
+| `Form.ErrorText` | `Fieldset.ErrorText` on the root                                                            | The form-level error.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
+
+Deliberately absent: `Positioner` and `Arrow` belong to floating surfaces and never appear here (a
+date picker's popover is inside its control); `Form.Section` and `Form.Group` are `Form.FieldSet`; the controls
+(`TextField`, `DateField`, `RefField`, …) are controls the dispatcher places in a `Form.Field`, not
+rows of their own. The dispatcher, `FormFieldDispatch`, maps a schema property to a control through
+the pure `resolveFieldRenderer` (annotation first, then format, then type) and renders the row once
+around it.
+
+Controls map onto `@dxos/react-ui` as: text, password, number → `Field.Input`; textarea and
+markdown → `Field.Textarea` / the editor; boolean → `Field.Switch`; date, time → `Field.Date`,
+`Field.Time`, `Field.DateTime`; literal options → `Select`; lookups and references → `Combobox`.
+
+## Examples
+
+### A schema-driven settings panel with one custom control and one unbound row
+
+```tsx
+<Form.Root schema={DeckSettingsSchema} values={settings} onValuesChanged={setSettings} autoSave variant='settings'>
+  <Form.Viewport>
+    <Form.Content>
+      <Form.FieldSet label={t('deck.label')} description={t('deck.description')}>
+        <Form.Fields exclude={['hue']} />
+      </Form.FieldSet>
+      <Form.FieldSet label={t('appearance.label')}>
+        <Form.Field path='hue'>
+          <HuePicker /> {/* useFormField(): { value, setValue } */}
+        </Form.Field>
+        <Form.Field standalone label={t('reset.label')} description={t('reset.description')}>
+          <Button onClick={handleReset}>{t('reset.button')}</Button>
+        </Form.Field>
+      </Form.FieldSet>
+    </Form.Content>
+  </Form.Viewport>
+</Form.Root>
+```
+
+The first field set holds the walker; the second is hand-written, but the bound
+`Form.Field path='hue'` still takes its label and description from the schema. The simplest form is
+`<Form.Root schema values><Form.Fields /></Form.Root>`, with no field set at all.

Removed in e5ab87e6 (+ dxos/edge#1030 `aa685f6`). You were right that it wasn't needed — and it turns out it never was.

It didn't break an existing contract; it was new on this PR. But it did widen one, and in the wrong direction: `requestAlarm` already existed on the concrete handle as part of the internal `requestSucceed`/`requestFail`/`requestSubmitOutput` family that backs `ctx.setAlarm`. What I'd done was promote it onto the public `Handle` interface, which is exactly the "alarms leak out of the process" you're objecting to. The one external consumer was edge's test-only `drain`, which armed an alarm before awaiting the handler. That turned out to be redundant: the agent already arms its own alarm on input (`onInput` → `ctx.setAlarm(0)`), so `runUntilSettled()` alone waits on the right thing. You're right, and this corrects my earlier reply on this thread. I said the losers "carry nothing the incoming patch does not also carry" — that only holds for the instant both rows are created. Afterwards each duplicate is found by some writer and takes its own updates, so one can hold `state: 'finished'` and its `finished` time while the survivor still reads `running`, and a bare heartbeat (which says nothing about state) would have deleted exactly that row.

Fixed in 6c3d204d. Duplicates are now folded into the survivor before removal, with explicit precedence:

- an end recorded anywhere is the end — a terminal `state` and its `finished` transfer to a non-terminal survivor;
- earliest `started`, because that is when the session actually began;
- latest `lastCheckedIn` carries `lastMessage` with it, since both describe one moment;
- `title`/`repo`/`branch`/`worktree` fill from whichever row has them.

The incoming patch is applied *after* the merge, so the newest report still wins wherever it speaks, and the terminal guard from the sibling thread then protects a state the merge just recovered.

Regression test `a duplicate carrying the end of the session is merged, not dropped`: the oldest row is `running`, the duplicate holds `finished` + `lastMessage` + a branch, and a bare `{ sessionId }` heartbeat drives it — without the merge the survivor would read `running`.

body:
Not applying this one — the proposed fix would break authentication rather than tighten it. Leaving the thread open in case a reviewer sees it differently.

`identity` here comes from `useIdentity()`, which is null on every first render until HALO resolves. So the early-return branch fires during normal boot, not only on reset. Clearing identity there would deauthenticate the **shared** `client.edge.http` — the same instance used for replication, queues and every other EDGE call — each time a container mounts before identity loads. That is a live regression, in exchange for the window below.

On the window itself:

- `setIdentity` already clears `_authHeader` and `_authAcquiredAt` whenever the identity actually changes, so a *different* identity can never inherit the previous one's header.
- `Client._close()` sets both `_edgeHttpClient` and `_edgeApi` to `undefined`, and `client.edge` is an invariant getter — so post-reset there is no path from the client to that instance.
- The residual case is a container still holding the object from the capability. The credential is a VP for the identity that just reset its own local storage, presented to its own account, so this isn't a cross-identity leak.
- This early-return shape is unchanged from the `useHubHttpClient` it replaces, so it isn't introduced here.

If the window is worth closing, the right place is `Client._close()` — clearing auth state on the instance it owns, where identity presence is not being inferred from a React render — not this effect. Happy to do that as a follow-up if you'd like it.

body:
Good catch — real bug, fixed in c20783eb.

The enrichment ran inside the method's own `try`, so a throw from the extractor was caught by the span's error handler: span marked errored, error rethrown, and a call that had already resolved became a failure. In the indexer that would have turned a completed pass into a fault — a blanket `invalidateQueries()` and a rethrow out of a `DeferredTask`.

The extractor now runs in its own `try`, so a fault costs the span its attributes and nothing else. Added a regression test asserting the method still resolves and the span is not marked errored (`tracing.test.ts`, 23 passing).

author: dmaretskyi
body:
Agreed on the direction, but they aren't redundant *yet* — they're doing two different jobs, and dropping either loses something today:

- **`withContext(ctx)`** supplies the parent span. `IndexEngine.update` marks itself with `Effect.withSpan`, which reads `Tracer.ParentSpan` out of the *Effect* context — it cannot see a DXOS `Context` passed as an argument. Without this the pass span has no children and we're back to parentless `IndexEngine.update` roots, which is the whole point of the PR.
- **the `ctx` argument** ends up as an abort signal. It threads `update` → `#update` → `source.getChangedObjects(ctx, …)` → `automergeHost.loadDoc(ctx, …)`, where its only use is bounding the readiness wait (`_waitForReady`'s `signal`). Effect interruption doesn't reach that: the call is wrapped in `Effect.promise`, so interrupting the fiber abandons the await but the underlying promise — and its subscription — keeps running. `FeedDataSource` ignores its `ctx` entirely.

So the redundancy is at the call site (same `ctx`, two paths in), not in what they do.

The unification you're describing is the right end state: have `withContext` provide the DXOS `Context` as an Effect service and drop the parameter from `IndexEngine.update` / `IndexDataSource.getChangedObjects`, so Effect is the single carrier. That's a signature change across `index-core` plus both data sources and their tests, so I've left it out of this PR rather than widening it — happy to do it as a follow-up, or now if you'd rather it land together.

body:
Confirmed and fixed in 41e9c5c9 — thanks, this was a real bug.

I verified against the live API rather than the docs alone. `GET https://api.deepseek.com/models` returns exactly three ids: `deepseek-v4-flash`, `deepseek-v4-pro`, `deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp`. `deepseek-chat` and `deepseek-reasoner` are gone, so both catalog entries would have failed at the provider.

The catalog now uses `deepseek-v4-flash` and `deepseek-v4-pro`. No translation layer at the EDGE boundary — the back-end name is deliberately the provider's own name, so a mapping would just hide the next rename.

Two consequences worth noting, both handled:

- V4 serves thinking and non-thinking mode from **one** model name (there is no separate reasoner id any more), and thinking is **enabled by default** with effort `high`. So `DeepSeekResolver` now sends `thinking: {type: 'enabled'|'disabled'}` explicitly — without it, a caller asking for `thinking: false` would silently get chain-of-thought and pay for it. This needed a small addition to `ChatCompletionsAdapter` (`RequestOptions.body`) to carry provider-specific request fields.
- The edge-side price table keyed the old names, so every request was falling through to a default rate. Fixed in dxos/edge#1037 with the V4 rate cards.

Added `Model.test.ts` to pin this: it asserts no DeepSeek entry uses the retired names and that every back-end matches `/^deepseek-v[0-9]/`, plus that every edge model carries a `service` marker so a future entry can't be silently claimed by the wrong resolver.

Also added a `manual`-tagged live suite (`DeepSeekResolver.test.ts`) — generate, streamed usage, thinking, and tool calls all pass against the real API.

author: dmaretskyi
body:
Fixed in 251c02ab, and this turned up something bigger than the finding described.

First, a correction to the premise: DeepSeek does **not** send a separate `choices: []` usage chunk. I captured a live stream (`stream_options.include_usage`, `deepseek-v4-flash`) and counted zero choices-less chunks — usage rides the *same* final chunk that carries `finish_reason: "stop"`. So the mechanism described here isn't what DeepSeek does.

But the conclusion was right anyway, via a different and worse route. The `finish` part was being emitted **twice**. OpenAI-format streams end with a `data: [DONE]` sentinel after the `finish_reason` chunk, and `parseStreamChunk` returns `{done: true}` for it too — so the loop emitted one finish with usage, then a second with `usage: {total: undefined}`. Any consumer reading the *last* finish part saw no usage at all. I confirmed it before touching anything: the live streaming test asserted one finish part and failed with `expected 2 to be 1`.

The fix covers both shapes. Usage is accumulated across chunks (last reported value wins) and the finish part is emitted exactly once, after the source drains:

- DeepSeek / Ollama — usage on the finishing chunk: unchanged, now emitted once.
- OpenAI proper — usage in a trailing `choices: []` chunk: folded in, since it arrives before the stream ends. This is the case you asked about, and it does now work.
- A stream truncated before any `finish_reason` still emits no finish part, rather than a synthetic one.

Regression fixtures added as requested, offline against a stubbed SSE body — `ChatCompletionsAdapter.test.ts` → `describe('streamed finish part')` covers all three sequences. I checked they're real guards: the first two fail against the pre-fix adapter and pass after; the third passes both ways, which is its point (it pins the no-synthetic-finish behaviour I could have broken).

This does touch the shared Ollama/LM Studio streaming path, unlike the Schema suggestion I declined earlier — the difference being that this is a correctness bug in the emitted output rather than a stylistic change to how a cast is validated.

Not taking this one, though the hang you describe is real.

The key table is rebuilt from the registered extensions on every call, so making registration depend on `DX_HUB_URL` would make the grammar itself depend on when the client finished loading: the same URL would parse before the config lands and stop parsing after. A URL's meaning should not move under it.

The real gap is the one behind your last sentence. A pair that resolution gave up on is indistinguishable, at the plank, from one that is still arriving, because `useNavigationPresence` cannot form a loader target for a singleton path and so answers `unknown` forever. That is true of any singleton key whose node is absent, not just these three, and the fix is for the projection's exhausted wait to be visible to the plank rather than for the grammar to flicker. Tracking it separately.

+---

Right about the risk, so fixed — but in dxos/dxos#13047, since #13045 merged before this landed.

Not the suggested diff: `timestamp ?? properties.commitSha` drops the commit from the seed whenever a timestamp exists, and one always does for `ci.boot-budget` (its timestamp *is* the commit date). That trades one collision for another — two commits sharing a committer date would then collide, and the commit-keyed rerun idempotency #12999 built this for would rest on a non-unique key. Seeded on both instead, plus the existing `dedup`.

One scope correction: the per-joiner uuids do not collide today. `dedup: joiner-N` already enters the seed, so a run's five joiner rows are distinct — verified in production, 5 rows / 5 uuids. The exposure was the run event alone.

Done — `src/Scorer.ts` is that DSL, and the eval's `dbQuery` is gone.

Each dimension now carries its own query, run against the space while it is still open (the runner scores in-scope, before the harness is disposed, and reports the query's value next to the mark):

- `Scorer.make({ name, description, query, score })` — any effect over the live space.
- `Scorer.database({ name, description, query: Query.select(…), score: (results) => … })` — as you wrote it.
- `Scorer.toolCalls({ … score: (invocations) => … })` — the session's tool calls paired with their results.
- `Scorer.duration({ targetMinutes, budgetMinutes, when, delivered })` — the wall clock, gated on the thing being timed having actually been produced.

`Scorer.once(key, effect)` shares what several scorers need (the artifact text, the MCP handshake with the deployed Worker) — memoized per run via a `Memo` service rather than at module scope, since variants run concurrently in one process.

`createEvalRunner` takes `scorers`, and `Scorer.toEvalite(SCORERS)` is the evalite side, so the list is declared once.

Fixed in `387e0e30` — the scope is now opened immediately before the `try` that closes it, so a host that dies after binding the listener still runs its finalizer. Kept it non-optional rather than the proposed `let scope … if (scope)`: `Scope.make()` itself can't fail, so the only gap was the host startup, and covering that keeps the type honest.

Two more from the same review, also in `387e0e30`:

- `send` is single-flight now (a second call while a turn is in flight is rejected instead of taking over the first one's callbacks), and a timeout goes through `#fail`, so a late `result` from the timed-out turn cannot land on the next one. Good catch — the conversation is one stream and the old code assumed a disciplined caller.
- JSDoc on `start`/`close`, and the `runClaudeEval` block moved above the function rather than above the middleware helper that had drifted between them.

Not doing the fourth (schema-decoding every stream event before storing it): the payloads come from the `claude` CLI this repo spawns itself, not from an untrusted peer, and drift surfaces immediately as a turn that fails its scorer rather than as a silent wrong answer — `Turn` reads three fields off events the CLI documents. A tagged-schema decode layer over that is a real change to a test driver's contract and belongs in its own PR if the CLI's stream ever proves unstable.

To be clear about the blast radius: `resyncDocument()` and `kickStalledSync()` themselves should stay. `#loadRootDoc` needs both, and for a real reason — `shareConfigChanged` only revives `all-failed`/`no-peers`, so a root that settled at `"succeeded"` without reaching `ready` is reachable only through the targeted call. -## 10. Diagnosing a non-converging document from logs
+- A fetch for a doc the peer doesn't have yet settles as **success-empty**, and the query goes
+  `unavailable`. Whether it later recovers depends on what the peer is:
+  - **A peer that is itself an automerge `Repo`** re-drives it. When that peer obtains the document
+    through its own query, `SubductionSource`'s `#save` triggers a sync round, and the waiting query
+    reaches `ready` with nothing re-asking from this side. Shown by `'a fetch answered before the
+relay has the document recovers when it arrives'` in `automerge-repo-subduction.test.ts` — note
+    that suite is `describe.skipIf(process.env.CI)`, so it is a local characterization, not a
+    CI-enforced pin.
+  - **The edge DO is not such a peer.** It has no `Repo` and no `SubductionSource`, so a document
+    pushed into its store by another device triggers no equivalent broadcast. Do not carry the
+    guarantee above across to EDGE; it has not been shown there.
+
+  Client-side re-ask mitigations for the EDGE case — a plain retry, repo-wide `shareConfigChanged`,
+  targeted `resyncSubduction`, and evicting the handle — were each measured against
+  `composer-app` `halo.spec.ts` at n=80 with `--retries=0`. None reduced the failure rate.
body:
Worth naming the cause here, since this null result is the strongest evidence in the PR and reads as an open question without it: all four mitigations failed because the divergence they were re-driving is [inkandswitch/subduction#286](https://github.com/inkandswitch/subduction/issues/286) — `heads_assuming_minimal` advertising fragment boundaries instead of fragment heads — so both peers already held identical bytes and no amount of re-asking could converge the advertised head sets.

Suggested addition after the measurement sentence:

> The cause is [inkandswitch/subduction#286](https://github.com/inkandswitch/subduction/issues/286): the edge advertises `getAllHeads()`, the host advertises materialized automerge heads, and on subduction <= 0.16.1 a boundary-less fragment makes the edge advertise a stale ancestor with no head in common. Re-asking cannot converge that; the fix is [subduction#290](https://github.com/inkandswitch/subduction/pull/290), unreleased as of 0.16.1. **Add no client-side measure until that release lands** — this row of null results is what the alternatives cost.

@@ -0,0 +1,155 @@
+name: Assistant evals
+
+# Runs every `@dxos/assistant-evals` scenario against the live model once a night and trends the
+# scores in PostHog, so a prompt or skill change that quietly degrades an agent shows up as a line
+# bending rather than as a complaint weeks later. Not part of `Check`: a scenario is a real agent
+# session against a real model, minutes long and non-deterministic, and its score is a sample to
+# plot, not a gate on a PR.
+#
+# Events go through `scripts/ci-event.mjs` as plain product-analytics events (`ci.eval.run`,
+# `ci.eval.result`, `ci.eval.score`), the same pipeline as `ci.boot-budget` and the EDGE nightly.
+# PostHog's LLM-analytics evaluations were considered and rejected for this: they grade live
+# `$ai_generation` traffic inside PostHog, and its offline-evaluation upload is an undocumented
+# endpoint that needs a personal API key rather than a project token. Dashboard: "Assistant evals"
+# in the Composer project.
+#
+# Secrets. The Anthropic key spends real money and the scenarios run whatever code the checkout
+# holds, so the job is shaped to keep the key away from anything a non-member can influence:
+#
+# - Triggers are `schedule` and `workflow_dispatch` only. No `pull_request`, so a PR never runs
+#   here, from a fork or otherwise; only someone with write access can dispatch, and what they
+#   dispatch is a branch they could already push to.
+# - The key is a dedicated Anthropic console key (`ASSISTANT_EVALS_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`) with its own
+#   spend limit, not the org-wide `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, so a leak is bounded and revocable without
+#   touching anything else. In Depot's secret settings it is limited to this workflow file and the
+#   `main` branch, so a dispatch of any other branch runs without it and stops at the guard below
+#   rather than leaking it to code that has not been reviewed onto main. Depot hydrates a secret
+#   into a step only where the YAML names it, and it is named on exactly one step.
+# - The PostHog key is the Composer project's ingestion token, which the app already ships to
+#   every browser; it is step-scoped anyway, and can only write events.
+# - `GITHUB_TOKEN` is `contents: read`, and the checkout does not persist it.
+#
+# What this does not defend against is a malicious change merged to main, which is the review
+# boundary, not this file's.
+
+on:
+  schedule:
+    # 03:00 UTC: after the EDGE nightly at 02:00 (the sandbox scenario reaches preview EDGE) and
+    # before the `Check` nightly at 04:00.
+    - cron: '0 3 * * *'
+
+  workflow_dispatch:
+    inputs:
+      models:
+        type: string
+        description: 'DX_EVAL_MODELS: comma-separated model variants for the scenarios that take them'
+        default: ''
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+  packages: read
+
+env:
+  # Bound once here rather than at the setup call site: a composite action cannot read the
+  # `secrets` context, but it does inherit the process environment.
+  MOON_CACHE_CA_PEM: ${{ secrets.MOON_CACHE_CA_PEM }}
+  MOON_CACHE_CLIENT_PEM: ${{ secrets.MOON_CACHE_CLIENT_PEM }}
+  MOON_CACHE_CLIENT_KEY: ${{ secrets.MOON_CACHE_CLIENT_KEY }}
+
+# Never `cancel-in-progress`: a run in flight is a night's sample, and losing it leaves a gap in the
+# series. A dispatch keys on its run id so two dispatches of one ref sample it twice.
+concurrency:
+  group: >-
+    ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.ref
+    }}-${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.run_id || '' }}
+  cancel-in-progress: false
+
+jobs:
+  evals:
+    runs-on: depot-ubuntu-24.04-8
+    container:
+      image: ghcr.io/dxos/gh-actions:24.11.1
+      credentials:
+        username: dxos-bot
+        password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
+    # Matches the `evals` task's own timeout (`.moon/tasks/tag-evalite.yml`): the longest scenario
+    # budgets an hour for the agent plus five minutes to grade what it left.
+    timeout-minutes: 90
+    defaults:
+      run:
+        working-directory: packages/core/compute/assistant-evals
+    steps:
+      - name: Checkout
+        uses: actions/checkout@v5
+        with:
+          fetch-depth: 0
+          filter: blob:none
+          persist-credentials: false
+
+      - name: Setup
+        uses: ./.depot/actions/setup
+
+      # Two scenarios drive the projected MCP server through the Claude Code CLI (`claude-harness.ts`).
+      # Unpinned on purpose, as the model alias is: the scenario scores the agent's effects through
+      # this repo's server, not a CLI version.
+      - name: Install Claude Code
+        run: npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code
body: Pinned to 2.1.259 and installed into a temp prefix on PATH (the image rejects `npm install -g` anyway). Integrity beyond npm's own lockfile-less install is not verified; a devDependency would give that via pnpm-lock, at the cost of a large package in the lockfile. Open to that if you think it is worth it.

+#   into a step only where the YAML names it, and it is named on exactly one step.
+# - The PostHog key is the Composer project's ingestion token, which the app already ships to
+#   every browser; it is step-scoped anyway, and can only write events.
+# - `GITHUB_TOKEN` is `contents: read`, and the checkout does not persist it.
+#
+# What this does not defend against is a malicious change merged to main, which is the review
+# boundary, not this file's.
+
+on:
+  schedule:
+    # 03:00 UTC: after the EDGE nightly at 02:00 (the sandbox scenario reaches preview EDGE) and
+    # before the `Check` nightly at 04:00.
+    - cron: '0 3 * * *'
+
+  workflow_dispatch:
+    inputs:
+      models:
+        type: string
+        description: 'DX_EVAL_MODELS: comma-separated model variants for the scenarios that take them'
+        default: ''
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+  packages: read
+
+env:
+  # Bound once here rather than at the setup call site: a composite action cannot read the
+  # `secrets` context, but it does inherit the process environment.
+  MOON_CACHE_CA_PEM: ${{ secrets.MOON_CACHE_CA_PEM }}
+  MOON_CACHE_CLIENT_PEM: ${{ secrets.MOON_CACHE_CLIENT_PEM }}
+  MOON_CACHE_CLIENT_KEY: ${{ secrets.MOON_CACHE_CLIENT_KEY }}
+
+# Never `cancel-in-progress`: a run in flight is a night's sample, and losing it leaves a gap in the
+# series. A dispatch keys on its run id so two dispatches of one ref sample it twice.
+concurrency:
+  group: >-
+    ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.ref
+    }}-${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.run_id || '' }}
+  cancel-in-progress: false
+
+jobs:
+  evals:
+    runs-on: depot-ubuntu-24.04-8
+    container:
+      image: ghcr.io/dxos/gh-actions:24.11.1
+      credentials:
+        username: dxos-bot
+        password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
+    # Matches the `evals` task's own timeout (`.moon/tasks/tag-evalite.yml`): the longest scenario
+    # budgets an hour for the agent plus five minutes to grade what it left.
+    timeout-minutes: 90
+    defaults:
+      run:
+        working-directory: packages/core/compute/assistant-evals
+    steps:
+      - name: Checkout
+        uses: actions/checkout@v5
+        with:
+          fetch-depth: 0
+          filter: blob:none
+          persist-credentials: false
+
+      - name: Setup
+        uses: ./.depot/actions/setup
+
+      # Two scenarios drive the projected MCP server through the Claude Code CLI (`claude-harness.ts`).
+      # Unpinned on purpose, as the model alias is: the scenario scores the agent's effects through
+      # this repo's server, not a CLI version.
+      - name: Install Claude Code
+        run: npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code
+
+      # The only step that sees the Anthropic key. `continue-on-error` so the summary, artifact and
+      # trend below run for a red night too, which is the night they are most needed; the last step
+      # turns the outcome back into the job's status.
+      - name: Run evals
+        id: evals
+        continue-on-error: true
+        env:
+          DX_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ASSISTANT_EVALS_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
body: Added a guard step before the key is named: it fails on a dirty tree (`git status --porcelain`) or a HEAD that is not the event's `github.sha`, which is exactly what a `depot ci run` patch produces. Documented in the header.

+# Delegating project tasks to an agent — data flow
+
+Source of truth is the code cited as `path:line`, as of the `task-visualization` branch. Where a
+table distinguishes "committed behaviour" from the "parallel change", the latter is that branch's
+idempotence guard and `assistant.delegationSpawned` event.
+
+## 1. Overview
+
+A reader checks rows in a project's task list and presses "Assign selected tasks to agent". One
+`ProjectOperation.DelegateTaskToChat` call creates a `Chat`, puts the tasks on its checklist, marks
+each task `started`/assignee `assistant`/reviewer = the reader, files the chat under the project,
+binds skills, opens the chat, and submits an opening prompt. `AgentService` spawns (or reuses) an
+`AgentProcess` bound to the chat; the prompt is enqueued on the chat's feed; the process runs a turn
+through `AiSession`; after every turn the supervisor `DelegationStrategy` reconciles the checklist,
+spawning one `RunInstructions` child process per ready `todo` agent task and folding each child's
+exit back into the task status and the feed. Trace events from every process land in the space's
+trace feed(s); the chat UI reads the feed, the `TracePanel` reads trace messages plus the process
+tree.
+
+```mermaid
+sequenceDiagram
+  actor User
+  participant PA as ProjectArticle
+  participant Op as DelegateTaskToChat
+  participant ECHO as ECHO (space db)
+  participant AS as AgentService / AgentProcess
+  participant DS as DelegationStrategy
+  participant Sub as RunInstructions (child process)
+  participant TR as Trace feed
+  participant UI as Chat / TracePanel
+
+  User->>PA: check rows, click delegate-tasks
+  PA->>Op: invoke { tasks: Ref[] }
+  Op->>ECHO: CreateChat (Feed + Chat + default Binding)
+  Op->>ECHO: chat.tasks.push; linkCompanion(project); db.add(chat)
+  Op->>ECHO: Task.setStatus('started'), assignee, reviewers, history
+  Op->>ECHO: Binding(skills, project) on chat.feed
+  Op->>UI: LayoutOperation.Open(project chat path)
+  Op->>AS: RunPromptInChat(chat, OPENING_PROMPT)
+  AS->>AS: getSession → spawn AgentProcess(target=chat URI)
+  AS->>ECHO: feed ← queued user Message
+  AS->>TR: AgentRequestBegin … CompleteBlock … AgentRequestEnd
+  AS->>ECHO: feed ← assistant Messages (incl. stats block)
+  AS->>DS: reconcile(chat, activeIds)
+  DS->>ECHO: sweep started/no-process → failed; todo+ready → started
+  DS->>Sub: invokeFiber(RunInstructions) → pid
+  AS->>TR: DelegationSpawned {taskId, pid} (parallel change)
+  Sub->>ECHO: own Feed; CompleteBlock events (parentPid = agent pid)
+  Sub-->>AS: onChildEvent(exited)
+  AS->>DS: onComplete(chat, taskId, exit)
+  DS->>ECHO: task.status = done|failed; feed ← notification Message
+  UI-->>User: chat renders feed; TracePanel renders spans + process tree
+```
+
+## 2. Step-by-step
+
+### 2.1 Checked set → operation
+
+| Step                       | Where                                                                                       | What                                                                                                                                                                           |
+| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
+| Checkbox toggles           | `packages/plugins/plugin-tasks/src/containers/TaskSetArticle/TaskSetArticle.tsx:155-165`    | `useSelection(taskSet.id, 'multi')` from `react-ui-attention`; keyed by the task set's id. Checkboxes render only when some plugin contributes `TasksCapabilities.TaskAction`. |
+| Toolbar reads the same set | `packages/plugins/plugin-projects/src/containers/ProjectArticle/ProjectArticle.tsx:273-310` | `useCheckedTasks` re-queries `Filter.childOf(taskSet)` and orders by the tree walk, so the handed-over list is in reading order, not tick order.                               |
+| `delegate-tasks` action    | `ProjectArticle.tsx:357-375, 402-412`                                                       | One invocation for the whole set: `DelegateTaskToChat { tasks: Ref[] }` with `{ spaceId }`; then `clear()` the selection. Disabled when the set is empty.                      |
+| Row action                 | `packages/plugins/plugin-projects/src/capabilities/task-action.ts:17-25`                    | `delegate-to-chat` ("Assign to agent") invokes the same operation with a one-element list.                                                                                     |
+
+### 2.2 `DelegateTaskToChat` — writes
+
+`packages/plugins/plugin-projects/src/operations/delegate-task-to-chat.ts`
+
+| Order | Write                                                               | Line             | Detail                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
+| ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
+| 1     | load tasks; resolve project                                         | 51, 68-75        | Project found by walking ECHO parents (`findProject`). More than one project → invariant failure, nothing written.                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
+| 2     | `CreateChat`                                                        | 77-81            | `packages/plugins/plugin-assistant/src/operations/create-chat.ts:31-64`: `db.add(Feed)`, `Chat.make({ feed })`, and a default `AiContext.Binding` appended to the feed (Assistant, Database, ChatContext, SkillManager, Alarm, Planning skills; `objects: [chat]`). Named after the task only when there is exactly one. |
+| 3     | `chat.tasks.push(refs)`                                             | 85-87            | Direct push — **not** `Chat.assignTasks` (`Chat.ts:122-138`), so no de-duplication. The field is non-owning (`Chat.ts:43-50`); tasks keep their task-set parent.                                                                                                                                                         |
+| 4     | `Chat.linkCompanion({ chat, subject: project })`                    | 91-93            | `Chat.ts:82-98`: appends `Ref(chat)` to `CompanionChatAnnotation` on the project and `Obj.setParent(chat, project)`.                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
+| 5     | `db.add(chat)`                                                      | 98               | Chat becomes durable in the space.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
+| 6     | per task: `Task.setStatus(task, 'started', { actor: reviewer })`    | 106-107          | `Task.ts:438` → `update` (`Task.ts:345-435`): sets `status`, pushes one `HistoryEntry { date, actor, event:'updated', description:'Status changed from todo to started.' }`.                                                                                                                                             |
+| 7     | per task: `assignee = { role:'assistant' }`, `reviewers = [reader]` | 108-116          | Bare role by design: `delegation-strategy` matches on `assignee.role`. `reviewers` non-empty is what later turns `done` into `review`.                                                                                                                                                                                   |

+Statuses: `todo | backlog | started | review | done | duplicate | blocked | cancelled | failed`

+
+Gating: `Task.isTaskReady` (`Task.ts:557-564`) — every `dependsOn` resolved within the checklist
+must be `done`; a dangling ref reads as satisfied. There is no automatic write of `blocked`; it is
+a manual status. `Task.isAgentWorking` (`Task.ts:551`) = `assignee.role === 'assistant' &&
+status === 'started'`, and drives the spinner glyph

+Observed consequence (no code path prevents it): a task delegated through this flow arrives at the
+first reconcile as `started`/`assistant` with an empty `activeIds`, so `sweepOrphanedTasks` marks
+it `failed` unless the opening turn already moved it to `review`/`done`. `findPendingTasks` never
+sees it either, since it only spawns `todo` tasks. See §7.
body:
Agreed this is real — it is documented as FLOW.md §7.1 precisely so the decision (restrict the sweep to ids this process spawned vs. leave delegated tasks `todo` for reconcile) is made deliberately; it changes the delegation model and is out of scope for this PR, which does not alter the sweep. Tracked in the project's TASKS.md.

_🤖 Addressed by [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)_

author: richburdon
body:
Not changed here: both writes happen on one client's ECHO database with no compare-and-swap to claim against, so ordering the status write before chat creation would only trade a rare double chat for a claimed task with no chat behind it. The toolbar disables the action while an invocation is in flight and drops rows the agent already holds, and the agent-side delegation verbs skip `started` tasks. A true atomic claim needs a runtime-side reservation, which is the same open question as FLOW.md §7.1.

_🤖 Addressed by [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)_

body:
Not a mismatch: `elevationProp` is an `ElevationLevel` (0–5, the surface ladder) while `useElevationContext` takes an `Elevation` ('base' | 'positioned' | …, the z-index/shadow axis), so the proposed call would not type-check. The two are independent axes and the content is styled exactly as `Popover.Content` styles them.

+# Delegating project tasks to an agent — data flow
+
+Source of truth is the code cited as `path:line`, as of the `task-visualization` branch. Where a
+table distinguishes "committed behaviour" from the "parallel change", the latter is that branch's
+idempotence guard and `assistant.delegationSpawned` event.
+
+## 1. Overview
+
+A reader checks rows in a project's task list and presses "Assign selected tasks to agent". One
+`ProjectOperation.DelegateTaskToChat` call creates a `Chat`, puts the tasks on its checklist, marks
+each task `started`/assignee `assistant`/reviewer = the reader, files the chat under the project,
+binds skills, opens the chat, and submits an opening prompt. `AgentService` spawns (or reuses) an
+`AgentProcess` bound to the chat; the prompt is enqueued on the chat's feed; the process runs a turn
+through `AiSession`; after every turn the supervisor `DelegationStrategy` reconciles the checklist,
+spawning one `RunInstructions` child process per ready `todo` agent task and folding each child's
+exit back into the task status and the feed. Trace events from every process land in the space's
+trace feed(s); the chat UI reads the feed, the `TracePanel` reads trace messages plus the process
+tree.
+
+```mermaid
+sequenceDiagram
+  actor User
+  participant PA as ProjectArticle
+  participant Op as DelegateTaskToChat
+  participant ECHO as ECHO (space db)
+  participant AS as AgentService / AgentProcess
+  participant DS as DelegationStrategy
+  participant Sub as RunInstructions (child process)
+  participant TR as Trace feed
+  participant UI as Chat / TracePanel
+
+  User->>PA: check rows, click delegate-tasks
+  PA->>Op: invoke { tasks: Ref[] }
+  Op->>ECHO: CreateChat (Feed + Chat + default Binding)
+  Op->>ECHO: chat.tasks.push; linkCompanion(project); db.add(chat)
+  Op->>ECHO: Task.setStatus('started'), assignee, reviewers, history
+  Op->>ECHO: Binding(skills, project) on chat.feed
+  Op->>UI: LayoutOperation.Open(project chat path)
+  Op->>AS: RunPromptInChat(chat, OPENING_PROMPT)
+  AS->>AS: getSession → spawn AgentProcess(target=chat URI)
+  AS->>ECHO: feed ← queued user Message
+  AS->>TR: AgentRequestBegin … CompleteBlock … AgentRequestEnd
+  AS->>ECHO: feed ← assistant Messages (incl. stats block)
+  AS->>DS: reconcile(chat, activeIds)
+  DS->>ECHO: sweep started/no-process → failed; todo+ready → started
+  DS->>Sub: invokeFiber(RunInstructions) → pid
+  AS->>TR: DelegationSpawned {taskId, pid} (parallel change)
+  Sub->>ECHO: own Feed; CompleteBlock events (parentPid = agent pid)
+  Sub-->>AS: onChildEvent(exited)
+  AS->>DS: onComplete(chat, taskId, exit)
+  DS->>ECHO: task.status = done|failed; feed ← notification Message

Partial blocks are ephemeral `PartialBlock` events only.                |

+### 2.4 Supervisor reconcile
+
+`packages/core/compute/assistant-toolkit/src/supervisor/delegation-strategy.ts`, called from
+`agent-process.ts:509-521` after each turn and `agent-process.ts:557-568` after each child exit.
+The strategy is contributed unconditionally by plugin-assistant
+(`packages/plugins/plugin-assistant/src/capabilities/skill-definition.ts:57`, consumed at
+`capabilities/agent-service.ts:39-46`).
+
+| Step                                  | Line                       | Write                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
+| ------------------------------------- | -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
+| `sweepOrphanedTasks(chat, activeIds)` | 91-110                     | Every checklist task with `assignee.role === 'assistant' && status === 'started'` whose id is not in `activeIds` → `status = 'failed'` (direct `Obj.update`, no history entry), then flush.                                                                             |
+| `findPendingTasks`                    | 71-85                      | `assignee.role === 'assistant' && (status ?? 'todo') === 'todo' && !activeIds.has(id) && Task.isTaskReady(tasks, task)`.                                                                                                                                                |
+| inherited skills                      | 131-137                    | Supervisor's bound skills minus `DelegationSkill`, read from the feed's bindings.                                                                                                                                                                                       |
+| per pending task                      | 143-178                    | `Database.add(Instructions { name: task.title, text, skills })`; `task.status = 'started'` (direct `Obj.update`, no history); `Delegation { id: task.id, spawn }`.                                                                                                      |
+| spawn                                 | `agent-process.ts:512-516` | `invoker.invokeFiber(RunInstructions, { instructions: Ref, input: {} })` → child pid; `delegations.push({ pid, id })`; `DelegationsCell.set` (KV under `process/<agentPid>/delegations`, 661-664); `Trace.write(DelegationSpawned, { taskId, pid })` (parallel change). |

+`activeIds` is the set of task ids in the in-memory `delegations` array, seeded from the KV cell at
+boot (`agent-process.ts:217`). The cell is scoped to the process id, so a fresh process starts empty.

+`packages/core/compute/assistant-toolkit/src/operations/run-instructions.ts`.
+
+| Property      | Value                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
+| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
+| key           | `org.dxos.operation.assistantToolkit.runInstructions` (operation process via `Process.fromOperation`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |

+| `environment` | inherited from the parent (`ProcessManager.ts:517-520`): `{ space, conversation: <supervisor feed URI> }`                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
+| trace meta    | `pid`, `parentPid`, `processName` set by `createProcessTraceService` (`process-trace.ts`); **`conversation` absent** — the strategy passes no `traceMeta`, and meta is not derived from `environment`                                                                                                                           |
+| feed          | a **new unparented `Feed`** in the space (`run-instructions.ts:98-105`), because the strategy passes no `chat`. Its messages are not in the chat's feed.                                                                                                                                                                        |
+| trace events  | `OperationStart { key, name:'Run Instructions' }` / `OperationEnd` (`packages/core/compute/compute/src/Process.ts:403-407`), `CompleteBlock` per block, `RequestPhase`. `OperationStart.name` is the operation's `meta.name`, **not the task title**; the task title is only on the `Instructions.name` object the child loads. |

+`agent-process.ts:541-570` → `delegation-strategy.ts:184-237`:

+| Write                                                                                   | Line                       | Detail                                                                                                                                                                     |

+| From                                                   | To      | How                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

+## 4. Task state machine
+
+Statuses: `todo | backlog | started | review | done | duplicate | blocked | cancelled | failed`
+(`packages/sdk/types/src/types/Task.ts:57-67`). Only the transitions below are written by this
+flow.

+| Transition                 | Writer                                                                     | Via                                                                                                                                                                                                         | History entry   |
+| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------- |
+| `todo → started`           | `DelegateTaskToChat`                                                       | `Task.setStatus(task,'started',{actor: reader})` (`delegate-task-to-chat.ts:107`)                                                                                                                           | yes, with actor |
+| `todo → started`           | supervisor reconcile                                                       | direct `Obj.update` (`delegation-strategy.ts:162-164`)                                                                                                                                                      | no              |
+| `started → failed`         | `sweepOrphanedTasks`                                                       | direct (`delegation-strategy.ts:103-108`) — any `assistant`-assigned `started` task not in `activeIds`                                                                                                      | no              |
+| `started → done \| failed` | `onComplete`                                                               | direct (`delegation-strategy.ts:194-196`) — ignores reviewers                                                                                                                                               | no              |
+| `* → review`               | any `Task.update`/`setStatus` asking for `done` on a task with `reviewers` | `finishStatus` (`Task.ts:335-336`) — planning `UpdateTasks` (`skills/planning/operations/update-tasks.ts:33`), tasks `UpdateTask` (`plugin-tasks/src/operations/update-task.ts:51`), the row's own checkbox | yes             |
+| `review → done`            | reviewer                                                                   | `Task.approve` (`Task.ts:445-446`) only                                                                                                                                                                     | yes             |
+| `todo` (assigned)          | delegation skill verbs                                                     | `delegate-task.ts:33-34`, `delegate-tasks.ts:58-64` set `assignee` + `todo`; `started`/`done`/`cancelled` are skipped                                                                                       | no              |

+Gating: `Task.isTaskReady` (`Task.ts:557-564`) — every `dependsOn` resolved within the checklist
+must be `done`; a dangling ref reads as satisfied. There is no automatic write of `blocked`; it is
+a manual status. `Task.isAgentWorking` (`Task.ts:551`) = `assignee.role === 'assistant' &&

body:
I tried the `Ref<Task.Task>` change and wrote the feed test you asked for — it says the trace feed does **not** handle refs correctly today, so this needs a decision before I push it.

What the test measured, with `task: Ref.Ref(Task.Task)` in the event and `Ref.make(task)` at both emission sites:

1. **The target is inlined.** What lands on the feed is
   `{"/":"echo:///01JGF…","target":{"id":"01JGF…","@type":"dxn:org.dxos.type.task:0.5.0","status":"started","title":"Roundtrip"}}`
   — a frozen snapshot of the task inside every status event. It goes stale the moment the task changes, and it grows each event by the size of the task.
2. **The DXN is space-less** — `echo:///<id>`, not `dxn:echo:<space>:<id>`.
3. **A ref read back has no resolver.** `Database.load(event.task)` dies with `invariant violation: Resolver is not set (ref.ts:612)`.
4. **In-process and feed consumers see different shapes.** `Trace.Event.data` is `Schema.Unknown`, so a live subscriber gets a `Ref` instance while a feed reader gets the encoded envelope; one `Schema.decodeUnknownSync(TaskStatusChanged.schema)` cannot read both — decoding the in-memory form returns nothing, which silently dropped every segment in the timeline unit tests.

Root cause is (4): `Event.data: Schema.Unknown` means nothing on the trace path encodes or rehydrates a ref.

Three ways forward:

1. **Keep `taskId`** (what is on this branch now, green) and file the trace-feed ref gap as its own issue. `Task.refEntityId` is all the timeline needs, and the id is what a stale snapshot would have given us anyway.
2. **Make `Event.data` schema-aware** — encode refs as bare DXN envelopes on write and rehydrate them with the reading database's resolver. That is the real fix and it is a change to `@dxos/compute`'s trace infrastructure, well beyond this PR.
3. **Carry a fully-qualified DXN string** instead of a `Ref` — resolvable by a feed reader, no snapshot, no infra change, but not a typed `Ref<Task.Task>`.

My recommendation is 1 now and 2 as a follow-up, since 2 is what makes refs work for every trace event rather than just this one. The `Ref` patch is ready locally either way — say which and I will push it.

author: dmaretskyi
body:
I built the `Ref<Task.Task>` change and wrote the feed test you asked for. It says the trace feed does **not** handle refs correctly today, so this needs your call before I push it. (I first posted this on the wrong thread — CodeRabbit's, above — and it answered; its vote isn't a substitute for yours.)

Measured with `task: Ref.Ref(Task.Task)` in the event and `Ref.make(task)` at both emission sites:

1. **The target is inlined.** What lands on the feed is
   `{"/":"echo:///01JGF…","target":{"id":"01JGF…","@type":"dxn:org.dxos.type.task:0.5.0","status":"started","title":"Roundtrip"}}`
   — a frozen snapshot of the task inside every status event: stale as soon as the task changes, and every event grows by the size of the task.
2. **The DXN is space-less** — `echo:///<id>`, not `dxn:echo:<space>:<id>`.
3. **A ref read back has no resolver.** `Database.load(event.task)` dies with `invariant violation: Resolver is not set` (`ref.ts:612`).
4. **Live and feed consumers see different shapes.** `Trace.Event.data` is `Schema.Unknown`, so an in-process subscriber gets a `Ref` instance while a feed reader gets the encoded envelope; one `Schema.decodeUnknownSync(TaskStatusChanged.schema)` cannot read both — decoding the in-memory form returns nothing, which silently dropped every segment in the timeline unit tests.

(4) is the root cause: nothing on the trace path encodes or rehydrates a ref while `data` is `Schema.Unknown`.

1. **Keep `taskId`** (this branch, green) and file the trace-feed ref gap separately. `Task.refEntityId` is all the timeline needs, and an id is what a stale snapshot would have yielded anyway.
2. **Make `Event.data` schema-aware** — encode refs as bare DXN envelopes on write, rehydrate with the reading database's resolver. The real fix, and a change to `@dxos/compute`'s trace infrastructure well beyond this PR.
3. **Carry a fully-qualified DXN string** instead of a `Ref` — resolvable by a feed reader, no snapshot, no infra change, but not a typed `Ref<Task.Task>`.

I'd take 1 now with 2 as a follow-up, since 2 is what makes refs work for every trace event rather than this one. The patch for the `Ref` version is ready locally — name the option and I'll push it.

body:
The pending set fills from the host's own `heads-changed`, so it also collects every document the worker loads from disk or receives from EDGE, not only local writes. On a reload every document of a space is ready within one 100 ms tick and ships as a single message.

Measured with the browser harness in this PR (3 spaces × 2000 objects, second client opening the worker's spaces, current branch otherwise unchanged):

| | with cap (500 docs / 1 MiB) | cap disabled |
|---|---|---|
| longest timer gap on the tab | 291 ms | 3228 ms |
| wall time until every space is queried | 12.1 s | 20.5 s |
| longest task | 0 reported | 147 ms |

Without the cap the whole space is one inbox drain: the slices keep individual tasks short, but `scheduler.yield()` continuations outrank timers, so the tab's timers are starved for the entire 3.2 s drain, and the worker cannot pipeline the next message while the tab integrates. Kept the cap.

Confirmed and fixed in `27cb08e`. The window is real: `new BroadcastChannel` at line 122, `await livenessLockGranted.wait()` at 137, `channel.onmessage` at 156 — and BroadcastChannel queues a delivery task rather than replaying to a listener attached later, so a displacement landing in between was dropped and `withPersistentStorage` would have waited out its full 10s for a worker that had already been asked to stand down.

The handler now goes up with `shutdown`, in the same synchronous block as the channel, so no delivery task can run before it is attached.

One thing your suggestion didn't cover, which the move exposes: if a displacement arrives *before* the liveness lock is granted, `shutdown` releases both locks while `run` is still awaiting the grant, and execution would then fall through to `endpoint.postMessage({type:'listening'})` — advertising a session from a worker that has already let go of its storage lock. So the await is followed by a `shuttingDown` bail.

`moon run worker-framework:build worker-framework:lint worker-framework:test` passes (5 test files), and the profile round trip still completes end to end after the change.

body:
Not taking this one — the guideline it cites doesn't apply here.

The rule is "never put untyped `Error` in an Effect **error type parameter**". `readDatabase` is a plain async function with no Effect anywhere in it, so there is no error channel for an untyped `Error` to leak into; it rejects a Promise, which is a different thing.

The surrounding module is uniformly async/Promise — `pickProfileArchive`, `stageProfileImport`, `applyStagedProfileImport` and `exportProfileArchive` all predate this PR in that style, and the callers are `useCallback` handlers in `SpaceTemplateToolbar` that `await` them inside `try/catch`. Converting one helper to Effect and running it at the UI boundary would leave the file half-and-half for no behavioural gain, in storybook-only code that ships to nobody.

`AGENTS.md` does say to prefer Effect over raw Promises, and a wholesale conversion of this module would be a reasonable follow-up — but it is a refactor of pre-existing code, not something this PR should carry.

Confirmed and fixed in `57673a8`. The per-document in-flight guard I added in `51d373e` only dedupes callers within one document, so two tabs booting together both saw the staged file, both read it before either took the lock, and the second would write its stale snapshot over everything the first one's client had done since applying the very same archive.

The lookup, read and validation now happen inside `withPersistentStorage`, with the presence re-checked while the lock is held.

One thing I kept outside the lock deliberately: a cheap `getFileHandle` existence probe before calling `withPersistentStorage` at all. Without it every ordinary boot would take the storage lock *and* broadcast a displacement, killing the worker of every other tab on each page load — a much worse regression than the race being fixed. The probe is only a fast path; the reading that decides anything is the one under the lock.

Not verified with two tabs — the recorded round trip drives a single page, so this rests on the code path rather than an observation, and I've said as much in the PR body.

`moon run stories-assistant:build stories-assistant:lint` passes, and the single-tab round trip still completes end to end after the restructure (identity and all four space ids restored, and the `Space is not initialized` rejection from the previous run is gone too).
